mechanisable: TIER A, pure static, no model call, runnable today. Together 771 of 2,013 failures = 38.3%.

Class 1, exam shape (246 failures, 12.2%). CHECK: for each practice item parse (command word, marks) from the command field or the leading word of the question plus the '(N marks)' suffix, and reject any pair outside the per-subject whitelist; reject Assess-10 in a Unit 3/4 section; reject 'Explain ... two/and ...' at 4 marks; for marks >= 8 reject guidance containing any '(N marks)' point allocation and require the strings Level 1-4 or Knowledge/Application/Analysis/Evaluation; require a non-empty context/stimulus field on every item. MEASURED: flags 198 of 215 live items (92%).

Class 3, MCQ construction (201 failures, 10.0%). CHECKS: chi-square the correctIndex distribution per section and per corpus and fail on skew (live corpus is 492/769 on index 1); reject any item where the correct option is more than 1.5x longer than the longest distractor; reject any item whose correct option contains a hedge word while the distractors are all absolutes; reject any stem beginning with an essay command word (Evaluate, To what extent, Discuss, Assess, Examine); reject duplicate options within an item; reject near-duplicate stems within a bank by token Jaccard; reject explanations containing '(A)' or 'option D' while options render unlabelled. MEASURED: 322 of 769 live items (42%) flagged.

Class 9, recall design, fill-in half (roughly 130 of 233). CHECK: reject any fill-in where a hint, stripped of punctuation, is a case-insensitive prefix of its answer, or where the hint's character count equals the answer's length; reject any reorder whose 'shuffled' permutation is one of the top-N already used in the corpus; reject any reorder/fill-in whose items or template are a set-match for a flow block in the same subsection. MEASURED: hint check fires on 141 of 141 live fill-ins against 130 known failures (100% recall, 92% precision); permutation check would fire on 99 of 131 reorders.

Class 8, wiring and surfacing (129 failures, 6.4%). CHECKS: every quiz and practice index must be referenced by exactly one block; every block must reference at least one quiz and one practice item; quizIndices must not be the identity sequence [0],[1],[2],...; every diagramRef must resolve to a diagram that exists; no section may ship with zero diagrams or zero recall widgets. MEASURED: would flag 648 orphan quiz items, 151 orphan practice items, 22 sections with sequential wiring, 3 dangling diagramRefs, 20 zero-diagram sections, 24 zero-recall sections.

Class 7, localisation (34 failures, 1.7%). CHECK: token denylist (Bank of England, HMRC, National Insurance, Consumer Rights Act, Trade Descriptions, CMA, Ofgem, Ofcom, Companies House, VAT, Brexit) plus a single-currency-per-section assertion. MEASURED: 26 of 43 sections carry UK-only tokens (130 occurrences), 16 of 43 mix currencies.

Class 12, spec numbering (17 failures, 0.8%). CHECK: meta.number must appear in a hand-built table of official IAL topic numbers per unit, and meta.title must match that number's heading. One 43-row table, written once.

Class 14, assessment-set coverage (14 failures, 0.7%). CHECK: a section's practice set must span the paper's command-word profile - at least one Define-2, at least one Calculate, at least one 6-mark Analyse, at least one levels-marked long item - and every content block must be the target of at least one practice item. MEASURED: 43 of 43 sections currently have no Calculate item.

BONUS pure-static check the audit under-counts: any sentence matching 'Examiners (reward|expect|penalise|deduct|frequently|often|will|test)' must carry a citation to a named mark scheme. MEASURED: 244 such sentences live, zero cited.
TIER B, static at gate time but needs a one-time reference asset built first. Together 541 of 2,013 = 26.9%.

Class 2, untaught assessment (296 failures, 14.7%). CHECK: extract every multi-word domain term from a quiz/practice/flashcard item and assert it appears in that section's own taught text (body, keyIdea, title, takeaway, examMatters, misconception, realExample). ASSET NEEDED: a cleaned controlled vocabulary; audit/raw/glossary_terms.json (372 terms, 301 multi-word) works as a first cut. MEASURED with that glossary: 145 of 769 quiz items flagged, precision by inspection roughly 70-80% (real hits include net profit margin, external economies of scale, expected value, payback period, corporate social responsibility, cash flow forecast, ethnocentric approach; noise includes generic phrases appearing only in a distractor). This is a triage list for a human or model, not a verdict.

Class 10, spec coverage gaps (169 failures, 8.4%). CHECK: for each section, assert every assigned spec bullet's key terms appear in the taught text. ASSET NEEDED: a machine-readable spec-bullet-to-keyword map derived once from audit/raw/econ_spec.txt and bus_spec.txt plus audit/raw/research-ial-spec-coverage.md. Once built the check is grep. This is the single highest-value asset to build because it also gates every future new section.

Class 6, off-spec content (76 failures, 3.8%). CHECK: denylist of frameworks that are not in the IAL specs (Porter's Five Forces for Business, VRIO, Bartlett and Ghoshal, Mendelow, Kotter, Lewin, Kay's distinctive capabilities, price elasticity of supply in Business, Giffen goods in Business) combined with the examiner-claim citation rule. MEASURED: 8 of 43 sections carry at least one denylisted framework name. ASSET NEEDED: the denylist itself, extractable in one pass from research-ial-spec-coverage.md lines 113-154.
judgementOnly: TIER C, needs reading comprehension or subject knowledge. Together 701 of 2,013 failures = 34.8%, and 68 of the 214 critical+high findings (32%).

Class 5, factual error in real-world examples (184 failures, 9.1%; 1 critical, 22 high). Requires world knowledge and a date-aware check of a named company claim. Examples that no string rule reaches: the Toyota JIT chip-shortage story is inverted; Tesla gigafactory financing is invented; Warby Parker described as 'direct distribution alone'; the eBay/Skype demerger never happened; Waitrose is claimed to have lost sales in 2008 when it gained share; Sony is claimed to have cut PS5 prices in 2024 when it raised them. A static rule can only ROUTE these - flag any realExample containing a named entity plus a year or a figure, which is most of them - not adjudicate them. This is the class where a student could repeat something to an examiner who knows the case.

Class 15, conceptual or definitional error in the taught prose (106 failures, 5.3%). The economics or business itself is wrong, with no external fact to check against. Examples: transfer payments taught as an injection into the circular flow; loan capital repayments listed as a fixed cost; an improvement in the terms of trade defined as an index above 100 rather than a rise; 'any deviation from competitive equilibrium reduces total surplus' stated in a section about externalities, where the equilibrium is itself the inefficient point; 'private markets produce zero public goods' contradicting the spec wording 'may not be provided'; a plc defined as a company that trades shares on the stock exchange. Catching these needs a reader who knows the subject.

Class 13, pedagogical structure and sequencing (161 failures, 8.0%). Flat difficulty ramps, blocks ordered against the spec, flow widgets that are feature lists rather than causal chains, misconceptions that are exam-technique tips, redundant blocks teaching the same idea three times, a concept taught in block 3 that block 1's recall already assumed. Partly amenable to cheap proxies (flow step count, subsection count per block, term-first-mention ordering) but the judgement 'is this actually a causal chain' is not.

Class 11, internal contradiction across surfaces (55 failures, 2.7%; 15 high). The section disagrees with itself: net profit and operating profit used interchangeably in body, flow, quiz Q0 and Q15; 'disruptive change' given four labels across content, notes, flashcards and a quiz explanation; a flashcard defining a quota as a non-tariff barrier while the quiz explanation says it is not. A model can diff definitions across surfaces, but deciding which one is correct needs subject knowledge. Some sub-cases are static (same term defined with different words in flashcards vs content), so this class is partly reclaimable.

Class 4, wrong or ambiguous answer key (29 failures, 1.4%; 2 critical, 7 high). Two defensible options, or the key is simply wrong. Examples: the PED gym question where revenue is exactly unchanged (500 x $40 = 400 x $50 = $20,000) yet the keyed answer says demand is inelastic so revenue rises, and the explanation contains a visible authoring note; a profit-maximising-supply item keyed to average total cost where the shut-down rule is average variable cost; a stratified-vs-quota sampling item where both options fit the stem. Arithmetic-recomputation catches a thin slice; the rest needs an examiner's eye.

Class 9 residual, reorder quality (roughly 103 of 233). The auditor's verdicts weak-or-arbitrary-sequence (48) and not-orderable (18) mean the four items have no real causal or temporal order, so the widget teaches an arbitrary permutation. Whether a set of four concepts has a genuine sequence is a judgement. Note that the permutation-reuse and copy-of-flow static checks would still block many of these items for a different reason.
The 63 unclassified records (3.1%) are mostly one-off subject-knowledge points and should be assumed to sit in this tier.

STRUCTURAL HONESTY POINT: detection is not repair. Every Tier A and Tier B check tells you an item is bad; none of them writes the replacement. Since the founder has also ruled that all questions be authored originally, the gate's output is a blocking signal plus a work queue, and the authoring itself stays in the judgement tier regardless of how good the checks get.

FAILURE TAXONOMY, 15 classes, n and share of the 2,013 failures. Built by ordered-regex classification of every audit record, verified by reading samples from each class; 63 records (3.1%) stayed unclassified, and class boundaries are approximate to about plus or minus 5%. (2) Assessment tests untaught material 296 (14.7%). (1) Wrong exam shape in practice questions 246 (12.2%). (9) Recall-widget design defects 233 (11.6%). (3) MCQ construction defects 201 (10.0%). (5) Factual errors in real-world examples 184 (9.1%). (10) In-spec content simply not taught 169 (8.4%). (13) Pedagogical structure and sequencing 161 (8.0%). (8) Wiring and surfacing defects 129 (6.4%). (15) Conceptual or definitional error in the taught prose 106 (5.3%). (6) Off-spec content presented as examined 76 (3.8%). (11) Internal contradiction across surfaces 55 (2.7%). (7) UK-centric framing for an international cohort 34 (1.7%). (4) Wrong or ambiguous answer key 29 (1.4%). (12) Section numbering does not match the spec 17 (0.8%). (14) Assessment-set coverage gaps 14 (0.7%).

THE MASS IS NOT WHERE THE FEAR IS. Classes 1+2+3+8+9 (exam shape, untaught assessment, MCQ construction, wiring, recall design) are 1,105 of 2,013 failures = 54.9%, and all five are structural/format defects. The class that feels most dangerous, factual error in real-world examples (class 5), is 184 = 9.1%. Severity-weighting does not change this: across the 1,075 records that carry a severity field, critical+high splits 84 pure-static / 62 static-with-asset / 68 judgement, i.e. 39% / 29% / 32%, almost identical to the count-weighted split.

HEADLINE MECHANISABLE FRACTION: 38.3% of failures (771 of 2,013) are catchable today by pure static checks with no model call and no new reference data. A further 26.9% (541) become catchable once three one-time reference assets exist (a spec-bullet keyword map, a corrected command-word table, an off-spec framework denylist) - still no per-section model call at gate time. That is 65.2% total. The remaining 34.8% (701) needs reading comprehension or subject knowledge.

PROVEN STATIC CHECK 1 - practice tariffs. I ran six pure-static rules over all 215 live practice items in audit/content-sections/*.json: 198 of 215 (92%) are flagged by at least one. Rule hit counts: no stimulus field 165, (command, marks) pair not in the IAL whitelist 123, no levels descriptor in guidance for an 8+ mark item 81, point-marked guidance on a levels-marked item 66, 'Explain two/and' multipart at 4 marks 46, Assess 10 used in a Unit 3/4 section where the exam uses Assess 12 21. The (command, marks) pairs actually used across the corpus are: Economics Define-4 x23, Explain-6 x23, Evaluate-20 x23, Outline-4 x23, Assess-10 x20, Analyse-10 x3; Business Explain-4 x20, Evaluate-20 x20, Assess-10 x19, Explain-6 x13, Analyse-6 x10, Define-4 x10, Outline-4 x7, Analyse-10 x1. Only 28 of 215 practice items carry a non-empty context/stimulus field at all.

PROVEN STATIC CHECK 2 - MCQ answer-position skew, the cheapest and highest-yield check in the corpus. Across all 769 live quiz items, correctIndex distribution is {0: 37, 1: 492, 2: 219, 3: 21}. 492 of 769 = 64% of every MCQ on the platform has answer B. A student who always picks option B scores 64% without reading anything. 30 of 43 sections have one index as the answer at least 60% of the time; business__resource-management is 23/25 on index 1, economics__supply 21/25, business__external-influences 21/25. This is a three-line check and the March validator did not have it. The auditor noticed it in only two sections (entrepreneurs-leaders, resource-management) and marked it critical there; it is in fact corpus-wide.

PROVEN STATIC CHECK 3 - fill-in hints leak the answer, 141 of 141. Every fill-in recall widget in the corpus encodes the answer in its hint. 125 leak on every blank, 16 on some; 70 also encode the exact letter count. Verbatim from audit/content-sections/business__the-market.json, subsection what-is-demand: hints ['ab__','mov_____','down____'] against answers ['able','movement','downward']. And business__entrepreneurs-leaders, creating-running-expanding: hints ['Cr______','Ru_____','Ex_______'] against answers ['Creating','Running','Expanding']. The auditor judged 130 of 141 fill-ins as failures (51 hint-leaks-answer, 65 trivial, 14 ambiguous-answers; only 11 'fine'), so a hint-is-a-prefix-of-the-answer check has 100% recall on the real failures at 92% precision.

PROVEN STATIC CHECK 4 - reorder widgets reuse six shuffle permutations. 131 reorder recall widgets across the corpus use only 6 distinct 'shuffled' arrays; (2,0,3,1) appears 56 times and (3,1,0,2) 43 times, so 99 of 131 (76%) use one of two permutations. A student who plays a handful learns the permutation rather than the sequence. This is a pure static check (count distinct permutations per corpus) and the auditor raised it in only one section's prose.

PROVEN STATIC CHECK 5 - quiz bank hygiene. Over 769 items: 322 (42%) are flagged by at least one of six pure-static rules. Correct option is more than 1.6x longer than every distractor: 146. Multi-word glossary term used in the item but absent from the section's own taught text: 145. Explanation refers to '(A)', '(B)', 'option D' although options render unlabelled: 45. Correct option hedged while all-but-one distractor uses an absolute (always/never/only/guarantees): 40. Essay command word used as an MCQ stem ('Evaluate...', 'To what extent...'): 28. Near-duplicate stem inside the same bank (Jaccard > 0.6): 22. One item has two identical options with only one keyed correct.

PROVEN STATIC CHECK 6 - wiring. 648 of 769 quiz items and 151 of 215 practice items are never referenced by any block's quizIndices/practiceIndices, so they only ever appear in random pre/post-test draws. 22 of 43 sections have quizIndices that are exactly sequential [0],[1],[2],... which is the auto-assignment signature behind the 'off by one' complaints. 55 of 170 blocks have no inline quiz and 106 of 170 have no inline practice. 20 of 43 sections have zero diagrams; 3 blocks carry a diagramRef into an empty diagrams[] array so InlineDiagram never renders. 24 of 43 sections have zero recall widgets of either type.

PROVEN STATIC CHECK 7 - localisation. 26 of 43 sections contain UK-only tokens (Bank of England, HMRC, National Insurance, Consumer Rights Act, Trade Descriptions, CMA, Ofgem, Ofcom, Brexit, VAT, Companies House), 130 occurrences in total. 16 of 43 sections mix pound and dollar figures inside one section. Target students are in HK/SG/MY/PK/LK/ME.

PROVEN STATIC CHECK 8 - unsourced examiner claims. 244 sentences across the 43 sections match the pattern 'Examiners reward/expect/penalise/deduct/frequently...'. Verbatim examples: 'Examiners reward structured VRIO analysis.' (business__assessing-competitiveness) and 'Examiners penalise students who calculate correctly but fail to interpret.' (same section). VRIO is not in the IAL spec at all. Not one of the 244 claims is sourced to a mark scheme. A static rule can require every such sentence to carry a citation, which converts an entire authoring habit into a blocking error.

ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED: the March validator at scripts/_upgrade-template.mjs checks only shape and string length. Its validate() function (lines 101-165) asserts blocks have a non-empty sections array, takeaway has at least 3 entries each at most 100 chars, keyIdea is at most 180 chars, and flow has between 2 and 4 steps. There is no check of command word, mark tariff, answer-index distribution, term coverage, index wiring or spec mapping. Every one of the eight checks above would have been additive to it.

THE APP'S OWN REFERENCE DATA IS CONTAMINATED AND WOULD POISON A NAIVE GATE. audit/raw/command_words.json lists 18 command words: Define, State, Identify, Calculate, Draw, Outline, Describe, Explain, Analyse, Assess, Evaluate, Discuss, Distinguish, Compare, Justify, Suggest, To what extent, Consider. Nine of those (State, Identify, Outline, Describe, Distinguish, Compare, Justify, Suggest, Consider) exist in neither IAL taxonomy, and two that do exist (Construct for Business, Examine for Economics) are missing. The correct sets, from audit/raw/research-ial-spec-coverage.md lines 136-138 and 151-154, are: Economics Define 2, Calculate 2 or 4, Draw 4, Explain 4, Analyse 6, Examine 8, Discuss 14, Evaluate 20 (no 10-mark, no Assess, no Outline); Business Define 2, Calculate 4, Construct 4, Explain 4, Analyse 6, Discuss 8, Assess 10 for Units 1-2 or 12 for Units 3-4, Evaluate 20. The command_words table must be rewritten before any gate reads it.

AUDIT RELIABILITY CAVEAT. The 2,088 content records are one model reviewer's judgements and were never adversarially verified. The code findings were: audit/raw/code-verdicts.json holds 88 verification verdicts on the 117 code findings (6 contested, 0 killed), per audit/README.md. This matters for the gate design: the same reviewer role that produced these numbers is the role being proposed as the replacement for the examiner, so its error rate is currently unmeasured. The static checks I ran above are the only numbers here that are independently reproducible from the live content.
evidence.notes:
Method. I classified all 2,088 records in audit/raw/content-audits.json (not content-work-flat.json, which is a critical+high filter and undercounts content work about 5x) by ordered regex over the auditor's own prose, then read samples from every class to check the assignments. 63 records (3.1%) resisted classification; class boundaries are approximate to about plus or minus 5% because several findings legitimately belong to two classes. Separately, and more importantly, I wrote and ran eight static checks against the 43 live section snapshots so the mechanisable claims rest on measurements of the real content rather than on keyword-matching the audit's descriptions. Those measurements are independently reproducible; the scripts are at /private/tmp/claude-503/-Users-arongijsel-Claude-APP/d75bd51f-ec0c-41fa-9577-e1d7e357143c/scratchpad/static_checks.py, sc3.py, sc4.py and sc5.py.

Where to aim the gate. 54.9% of all failures sit in five structural classes (exam shape, untaught assessment, MCQ construction, wiring, recall design) that have nothing to do with subject expertise and everything to do with the absence of any check beyond string length. 38.3% of all failures are blockable today with code that needs no model call, no budget and no reference data; 65.2% once three one-time assets exist. The severity-weighted picture is the same to within three points, so the gate should be aimed at format and coverage first, not at fact-checking first. That is the opposite of where intuition points.

Three honesty caveats the parent should carry forward. First, the audit is unverified: the 117 code findings got 88 adversarial verdicts (audit/raw/code-verdicts.json) but the content audit got none, so 453, 398 and 224 are one reviewer's claims. The same reviewer role is the one being proposed as the examiner's replacement, and its error rate is currently unmeasured; the 2,088 labels are the obvious calibration set for fixing that. Second, no static check reaches the 34.8% judgement tier, and that tier contains the failures with the worst student-facing consequence - a student repeating the inverted Toyota JIT story or the invented Tesla financing to an examiner who knows the case. A gate that scores 65% on volume scores 0% on that specific risk. Third, the app's own reference tables are part of the failure: audit/raw/command_words.json contains nine command words that exist in neither IAL taxonomy and is missing two that do. Any gate that reads the database's own vocabulary inherits the March bug. Fix the reference data before building the gate on top of it.

One unasked-for finding worth escalating: 492 of 769 MCQs have correctIndex = 1, so always picking option B scores 64% platform-wide. The auditor caught this in two sections; it is corpus-wide, it is a three-line check, and it makes the quiz bank's reported scores close to meaningless as a mastery signal right now.

(subject, unit, command, marks) appears in the observed tariff table with at least 2 sightings — this alone rejects 173 of the current 215 items
ao_split integers sum exactly to marks, and match the observed shape for that (subject, unit, command, marks) tuple
marking_mode is 'points' or 'levels' and agrees with the observed mode for that tuple

for levels items: stimulus is present and non-empty above a minimum word count — currently 62 items would fail
for point-marked items: the model answer carries (1K)/(1AP)/(1AN)/(1EV) credit tokens and the token counts equal the declared ao_split
command word is in the observed set for that subject — kills State, Identify, Outline, Describe, Distinguish, Compare, Justify, Suggest, Consider
Business Evaluate 20 rubric text contains an explicit recommendation/solution requirement; Economics 20-mark items carry a context line
Draw (Economics) / Construct (Business) items reference an actual diagram asset, and any item whose ceilings include a diagram cap has that diagram
'two' in the stem implies exactly two developed strands in the model answer, and a 'credit the best two' ceiling

I issued a ranged curl against all 86 distinct URLs: 86/86 returned HTTP 200. All 86 PDFs downloaded (37MB) and extracted cleanly with `pdftotext -layout` — none under 3,000 characters, so the corpus is born-digital text, not scans.

Asymmetry that shapes everything: only 11 of 75 slots have BOTH the question paper and its mark scheme (WEC11 Jan-2023, Jan-2024, Oct-2022, Oct-2024; WEC13 Jun-2021, Jun-2022; WBS11 Jun-2021, Oct-2022; WBS12 Jun-2021, Jan-2024; WBS14 Oct-2021). WEC14 has 9 mark schemes and 0 question papers. The latest paper in the table is October 2024; nothing from 2025 or 2026.

What a mark scheme does and does not give you. It DOES give: the question stem verbatim in the table header row (Sections B/C/D), the question number, the AO split written out as words ("Knowledge 1, Application 3"), the Quantitative Skills codes, indicative-content bullets, full level-descriptor grids with band boundaries, and ceiling rules. It does NOT give: Section A multiple-choice question text or options (that table shows only the answer letter plus distractor rationales), and it does not reproduce the extract, figure or data the question hangs on. So MCQ shape and stimulus shape can only be calibrated from the 14 question papers.

An anchor index is buildable today with zero model calls. A naive regex parser over the 72 extracted mark schemes recovered 284 question records, 281 of them with a usable stem, from 58 of the 72 files. Anchors per subject/unit: Business U1 41, U2 56, U3 25, U4 49; Economics U1 33, U2 46, U3 17, U4 14. The parser is lossy — 14 files yielded nothing because the 'Question' header spacing varies between one and several spaces between PDF vintages — so the table needs one reconciliation pass before it can BLOCK a write, or it will reject valid items.

Point-marked vs levels-marked, measured across all 72 mark schemes rather than taken from the spec appendix. Point-marked (integer AO counts, no grid): Economics Define 2 (K2), Explain 4, Draw 4 (K1/A3), Calculate 4 (K1/A3), Analyse 6 (K2/A2/An2), Examine 8 (K2/A2/An2/Ev2); Business Define 2 (K2), Explain 4, Calculate 4, Construct 4 (K1/A2/An1), Analyse 6 (K2/A2/An2). Levels-marked: Economics Discuss 14 and Evaluate 20; Business Discuss 8, Assess 10 (U1/U2), Assess 12 (U3/U4), Evaluate 20.

The two subjects mark levels on structurally different machinery, and an author who does not know this will produce Business-shaped Economics items. ECONOMICS splits a levels question across TWO separate grids: Discuss 14 = a KAA grid of 3 levels (1-3 / 4-6 / 7-8) plus an Evaluation grid of 3 levels (1-2 / 3-4 / 5-6); Evaluate 20 = a KAA grid of 4 levels (1-3 / 4-6 / 7-9 / 10-12) plus an Evaluation grid of 3 levels (1-3 / 4-6 / 7-8). BUSINESS uses ONE combined KAAE grid: Discuss 8 = 3 levels (1-2 / 3-5 / 6-8); Assess 10 = 4 levels (1-2 / 3-4 / 5-7 / 8-10); Assess 12 = 4 levels (1-2 / 3-4 / 5-8 / 9-12); Evaluate 20 = 4 levels (1-4 / 5-8 / 9-14 / 15-20). These band boundaries were identical in every sighting (e.g. Business Assess 12 n=25 across U3 and U4, Economics Evaluate 20 n=45).

What the level descriptors turn on. The Economics KAA axis moves precision of knowledge -> application carrying contextual evidence -> 'logical and multi-stage chains of reasoning in terms of cause and/or consequence'. The Economics EVALUATION grid runs on a different axis entirely: generic evaluative comment -> 'evaluation of alternative approaches' -> 'recognises different viewpoints and/or is critical of the evidence', each band additionally gated on supporting evidence and a logical chain. Business bundles all four AOs into one ladder whose top band uniquely requires 'an effective conclusion that proposes a solution and/or recommendations' — that recommendation requirement is Business-only and only at Evaluate 20.

The same command word does not fix the tariff or the grid. WBS11 October 2022 Q1(e) is an 'Analyse' question worth 10 marks marked on the four-level Assess-10 grid, which the spec's Appendix 6 command-word table does not predict. This is the reason the tariff table has to be seeded from the observed corpus rather than from the appendix: the checkable unit is the (subject, unit, command, marks, grid-shape) tuple, not the command word.

Subject-specific AO splits that an AI author will get wrong by default. Business Explain 4 was K1/A2/An1 in 12 of 12 sightings. Economics Explain 4 was K1/A1/An2 in 9 sightings and K2/A2/An0 in 7 (the second shape is the 'explain the difference between X and Y' variant). So the AO split cannot be a single global rule per command word — it has to be carried per anchor.

Point-marked schemes tag each credit inline with tokens: (1K) 226 times, (1AN) 240 times, (1AP) 39 times across the corpus. That makes the authored guidance mechanically auditable — require the same tokens in the model answer and assert that the counts equal the declared AO split.

Ceiling rules are explicit and countable, and are the main way a levels question is capped. Across the corpus: ~15 'NB ... maximum of Level 3' lines tied to a missing diagram, 9 tied to missing application or missing reference to the named context, plus 'if more than two barriers considered, credit the best two'. Any authored levels item therefore needs an explicit ceilings field, not prose.

The current 215 authored practice items fail on shape, measured not asserted. Fields actually present: question 215/215, marks 215/215, guidance 215/215, command only 165/215 (50 items carry no command word at all), context key 50 but non-empty only 28. Scoring each item's (subject, unit, command, marks) against pairings seen at least twice in the real corpus: 42 of 215 match, and all 42 are either Evaluate 20 (33) or Business Assess 10 (9). 173 of 215 do not match any real pairing.

The sharper number: 0 of 215 items both match a real tariff AND carry a non-empty stimulus. 62 items use a levels-marked tariff with no stimulus whatsoever. Every levels-marked question in the real corpus is anchored to an extract, figure or named business, so an unstimulated Evaluate 20 cannot be marked on the real grid at all — the Application strand has nothing to bite on.

The app's own command-word reference teaches the wrong exam. audit/raw/command_words.json holds 18 rows including State, Identify, Outline, Describe, Distinguish, Compare, Justify, Suggest and Consider. State, Identify, Outline and Describe have 0 sightings across all 72 mark schemes. Its Draw entry also instructs students to show the 'deadweight loss area', terminology the spec research already flagged as non-IAL (the spec says welfare loss/gain areas).

The March validator never looked at questions. `validate()` at line 101 of /Users/arongijsel/Claude APP/economics-next-remediation/scripts/_upgrade-template.mjs checks array lengths and character counts only — keyIdea <= 180 chars, takeaway <= 100 chars, flow steps <= 4, sections non-empty. It does not read practice[] at all. Nothing about tariffs, command words or mark schemes was ever checkable.

Copyright, the live exposure. Both artefact types carry explicit notices: mark schemes state 'All the material in this publication is copyright' / '(c) Pearson Education Ltd 2023'; question papers carry '(c)2023 Pearson Education Ltd.' plus an Acknowledgements section, meaning some extract material is third-party licensed in and is not Pearson's to sublicense onward. The founder is currently redistributing 86 Pearson-copyright PDFs from a world-readable URL. That is a distribution act independent of anything the citation discipline does, and it is the largest copyright exposure in this slice.
evidence.notes:
THE CITATION DISCIPLINE, AND THE EXACT FIELDS

Rule: no authored item may be written, and none may be published, without naming a real paper and question it is modelled on. The anchor is metadata about a real assessment, not content from it.

Required fields on every authored item:

IDENTITY — item_id; section_slug; spec_point (a real heading in the spec text); subject; unit.
ANCHOR — anchor_paper_id (FK to past_papers); anchor_code (WEC11..WBS14); anchor_session; anchor_year; anchor_question (e.g. "12(e)"); anchor_provenance ("MS+QP" for the 11 complete slots, "MS-only" for the other 61); anchor_verified_at.
SHAPE COPIED FROM THE ANCHOR (facts and formats, not expression) — command; marks; marking_mode ("points" | "levels"); ao_split {K, A, An, Ev} summing to marks; level_grids (for Economics two grids, for Business one) each as {name, levels, bands}; qs_codes; ceilings (e.g. "max Level 3 if no diagram"; "credit the best two"); requires_diagram; requires_recommendation.
ORIGINAL CONTENT (must not resemble the anchor) — question_text; stimulus {origin: "authored", body, figures, source_note} — mandatory whenever marking_mode is "levels"; model_answer with (1K)/(1AP)/(1AN)/(1EV) tokens for point-marked items, or per-level exemplars for levels items; indicative_points (authored); misconception_note.
COPYRIGHT ATTESTATION — similarity_max (highest n-gram overlap against the extracted corpus); scenario_domain (must differ from the anchor's); reviewed_by; reviewed_at.

THE COPYRIGHT LINE, EXPLICITLY

May be read: all 86 PDFs, freely, for analysis. Reading is not distribution.
May be imitated, because these are facts, formats and ideas rather than protected expression: the command word; the mark tariff; the AO split; the number of levels and the band boundaries; the structural shape of a question slot ("define a term from the extract, 2 marks"; "analyse two reasons, 6 marks"); the topic; the QS codes; the requirement to reference an extract; the "credit the best two" convention; diagram and recommendation requirements; the ceiling rules.
May NEVER be copied: the question stem or any recognisable fragment of it; the extract, figure, table or data values; the named company, country or scenario the paper used; indicative-content bullets (expressive prose); level-descriptor wording verbatim — paraphrase the criteria into house language for the student-facing rubric; MCQ distractor rationales; and above all, the PDFs themselves must not be served to students.
Banned by rule because the grey zone is not worth arguing: a stem rewritten with only the company name and the numbers changed. Require a different scenario domain and independently authored data, and enforce it with the n-gram check.

ACT ON THIS FIRST, SEPARATELY FROM THE GATE: the past-papers bucket is world-readable and currently redistributes 86 Pearson-copyright PDFs to anyone with the URL. Make the bucket private and have the pipeline read it with the service key. This is a distribution exposure that exists whether or not the citation discipline ships, and no amount of careful authoring offsets it.

WHAT THIS GATE CANNOT DO — be honest with the founder

It makes items exam-shaped. It does not make them correct: the 453 accuracy issues are untouched by every check in the mechanisable list.
The corpus stops at October 2024, so it cannot reflect any later change to papers or spec.
For 61 of 72 mark schemes there is no matching question paper, so the anchor gives marking shape without the question that shape was built for. Those anchors must be flagged and must force an authored stimulus.
The parser is lossy today (58 of 72 files yielded items), so the tariff table needs one reconciliation pass before it BLOCKS writes.
Most importantly: every mechanical check is cheap to satisfy and cheap to game. An AI author can hit the tariff, the AO split, the band boundaries and the token counts and still write a question no examiner would set. The judgement list is where the real risk lives, and the founder's scarce attention should be spent there — on whether the stimulus supports the question and whether the reasoning chains are real — not on re-checking anything a script already proves.

judgementOnly: Whether a factual claim is TRUE. The critical accuracy issue on `the-market` is a realExample about UK strawberry farmers that passes every one of the 16 March checks — right length, named entity, has misconception and examMatters — and teaches the law of supply backwards (it attributes summer supply to high retail prices when summer prices are lowest; seasonality is a shift, not a movement along the curve). No string check can see this.

Whether a multiple-choice item has exactly ONE defensible answer. The audit's quiz item on `meeting-customer-needs` q3 is keyed to 'stratified' but quota sampling also fits the stem, because the only real discriminator (random vs non-random selection within groups) is absent. Detecting this requires reasoning about the option set against subject knowledge.

Whether a mark scheme's credit allocation is how an examiner would actually award. The numbers can be made to sum to the tariff (checkable) while crediting things an examiner would not credit — e.g. the audit's finding that a 4-mark 'define niche market' guidance pads with an example and 'premium pricing', neither of which belongs in a definition.

Whether a section actually TEACHES a spec sub-topic, versus merely containing its vocabulary. A term-presence scan proves absence; it cannot prove presence of correct teaching. 'capital goods' appearing once does not mean capital vs consumer goods is taught.

Whether the content is original rather than paraphrased from a copyrighted source. Given the founder's copyright constraint this matters, and no static check establishes provenance — you can only compare against a corpus you hold.
Whether difficulty, sequencing and cognitive load are right for a first-time student, and whether a 20-mark answer plan would actually reach the top level descriptor.
Whether examples are current and appropriate for an international cohort rather than UK-centric (the platform's audience is IAL, not UK GCE).
Whether an explanation resolves the misconception it names, or merely asserts the correct answer more loudly.
Whether a diagram's labels, axes and shifts match the accompanying prose.

findings: WHAT IT CHECKED — exactly 16 conditions, all shape. scripts/_upgrade-template.mjs validate() (lines 118-180) checks: per block — title non-empty, sections[] non-empty array, takeaway[] array with >=3 items, each takeaway <=100 chars; per subsection — id present, id unique within the file, title present, keyIdea present, keyIdea <=180 chars, keyIdea contains no '**', body[] non-empty array, each body item has SOME 'type' value, flow has >=2 steps, flow has <=4 steps, flow resultType in {good,bad,neutral}, realExample.text present, misconception present, examMatters present. That is presence, array length, string length, one enum and one uniqueness test. Nothing else.

IT IMPLEMENTED ONLY THE SUBSET OF ITS OWN RULEBOOK THAT `.length` COULD EXPRESS. The template's header comment (lines 9-21) states five more rules that the code never checks: 'body paragraph — max 3 sentences', 'realExample — real named entity, 2-3 sentences, starts with entity name', 'misconception — 3 sentences: wrong claim -> why wrong -> what to write instead', 'examMatters — 2-3 sentences on what the examiner specifically awards', and the supported body-type list ('paragraph'|'subheading'|'flow'|'bullets' — the code checks that `type` EXISTS, never that it is one of these). Measured against live content: 136 of 1,110 paragraphs (12%) break the documented 3-sentence rule; 24 of 413 realExamples have no capitalised name in their first sentence. Both rules were prose in a comment, so both were violated in production.

IT ONLY EVER SAW ONE OF THE EIGHT CONTENT TABLES. validate() is called on CONTENT, which is written to section_content. Across the whole repo no validate() function is ever applied to section_quiz, section_practice, section_notes, section_flashcards, section_diagrams, section_extras or section_common_mistakes (grep 'function validate' over scripts/, seed/, audit/scripts/ returns 22 files, all of them section_content upgrade scripts plus the template). That is the direct mechanical explanation for 398 quiz issues and 215 practice issues surviving alongside a 'validator': the tables carrying them were never in scope.

HALF THE SCRIPTS SKIPPED IT, AND THE SPLIT IS EXACTLY VISIBLE IN LIVE CONTENT. There are 43 scripts/upgrade-content-*.mjs — one per live section. 21 contain the validate() function; 22 do not. I re-ran the March validate() verbatim over all 43 live section_content payloads in audit/content-sections/*.json: 21 PASS, 22 FAIL, 179 errors. The 22 failing sections are a perfect 1:1 match with the 22 scripts that lack validate() (assessing-competitiveness, business-growth, business-objectives-strategy, decision-making-techniques, global-industries-mncs, global-marketing, global-markets-expansion, globalisation, influences-business-decisions, managing-change, balance-payments-exchange-rates, causes-effects-globalisation, government-intervention-firms, growth-development, introductory-concepts, labour-markets, market-structures-contestability, poverty-inequality, revenue-costs-profits, role-state-macroeconomy, trade-global-economy, types-sizes-businesses). The validator was 100% effective on the rules it checked, on the sections that chose to run it, and 0% everywhere else. Copy-paste-a-function is not a gate; it is an opt-in.

PASSING THE VALIDATOR HAD ZERO CORRELATION WITH QUALITY. Cross-referencing that pass/fail split against audit/raw/content-audits.json: the 21 sections that PASS the March validator today are graded C, C, C ... all 21 are grade C, and they carry 246 of the 453 accuracy issues. The 22 that FAIL carry 207 (17 C, 5 D). The sections that satisfied every shape rule hold MORE accuracy debt than the ones that did not. A green validator run told you nothing about whether the content was true.

THE MOST EXPENSIVE OMISSION WAS ONE LOOKUP TABLE. A (command, marks) pair check against the tariff table in audit/README.md would have rejected 173 of 215 live practice questions (80%) with no model call. Breakdown computed from audit/content-sections/*.json: 123 questions carry a command/tariff pair that does not exist in IAL (Define@4 x33 — IAL Define is 2; Explain@6 x36 — IAL Explain is 4; Outline@4 x30 — 'Outline' is not an IAL command word at all; Assess@10 x20 in Economics — 'Assess' does not exist in IAL Economics; Analyse@10 x7 — IAL Analyse is 6), and a further 50 (all of Business Units 3 and 4) have no `command` field whatsoever. Only 42 of 215 have a pair that is valid by the audit's own table (23 econ Evaluate@20, 9 bus U1-2 Assess@10, 10 bus U1-2 Evaluate@20). Note this refines the audit README's headline: the README says all 215 use non-existent tariffs; a pure pair check clears 42 of them, so those 42 fail on grounds that need judgement, not arithmetic.

OFF-SPEC TERMINOLOGY WAS A GREP AWAY. Terms that appear ZERO times in the official Pearson IAL Economics spec (audit/raw/econ_spec.txt) appear this often in the 23 live Economics sections: 'deadweight' 143 hits in 9 sections, 'merit good' 148 hits in 4 sections, 'demerit good' 51 in 4, 'accelerator' 75 in 3, 'nudge' 31 in 2, 'bounded rational' 21 in 6. These are UK GCE leftovers taught to IAL students. A subject-keyed blocklist derived from the spec text — which is already in the repo — catches all of them with no model call.

QUIZ ITEMS CARRY A MEASURABLE ANSWER-LENGTH GIVEAWAY. Across 769 live quiz items (all 4-option): in 474 of them (62%) the keyed correct answer is the single longest option. Chance is ~25%. A student who ignores the economics and always picks the longest option scores 62%. Also measurable with no model call: 435 of 769 explanations never restate the keyed answer text, 1 item has duplicate options. Meanwhile correctIndex is in range in all 769 and every item has a non-trivial explanation — so the cheap structural checks were already satisfied while the item quality was not.

THERE IS A SECOND, COMPLETELY UNGUARDED WRITE PATH THAT NO ONE HAS COUNTED. app/api/admin/sections/[id]/[type]/route.js is a live PUT endpoint that writes arbitrary JSON into any of the eight content tables via TABLE_MAP. Its only checks are: user is signed in, user.app_metadata.role === 'admin', and the type string maps to a known table. It then calls restoreIds() (a thoughtful id-preservation routine) and writes. There is no content validation at all. Upstream, the only validation in components/admin/SectionEditor.jsx is `JSON.parse` at line 818 — the error state is literally the string 'Invalid JSON'. Any validator bolted onto the scripts is bypassed entirely by one paste into the admin textarea.

THE CLIENT IS NOT A CHOKEPOINT TODAY, BUT IT IS ONE EDIT AWAY FROM BEING ONE. 93 of 96 files in scripts/ import the shared client from scripts/_db.mjs. Only 3 build their own (_fix-keys.mjs, add-ppf-labels.mjs, upload-diagrams.mjs). But ALL 10 seed/ scripts build their own createClient by reading .env.local directly (seed.mjs, seed-content.mjs, seed-economics-practice.mjs and 7 others), and 4 of 5 audit/scripts do too — including the remediation-era audit/scripts/hotfix-packet-0-content.mjs (line 20), which means the bypass habit is still live in September, not just a March artefact. lib/supabase-server.js exports a third, separate service-role client used by the API routes.

THERE IS NOWHERE ELSE TO HANG A GATE. The repo has no .github/, no .husky/, and no non-sample hooks in the worktree's git hooks directory. package.json has exactly three guard scripts (contrast, quant-check, pin-check) and no test runner; PROTOCOL.md section 2 states outright 'There are no tests in this repo; the build is the floor.' So 'run the validator in CI' is not an available option — the gate has to live in the process code that performs the write.

THE PLAN ALREADY NAMES THIS AS THE DECISION. audit/PLAN.md line 94 (packet 3) specifies checks 'placed inside the write path' and its justification column reads: 'A gate beside the write path is a convention. March had one of those.' Meanwhile audit/PROTOCOL.md gate step 4 currently says 'Validator green on all 43 sections (from packet 3 onward)' — which is an after-the-fact sweep, i.e. exactly the convention PLAN.md warns about. Both need to exist, but the sweep must not be mistaken for the gate.
evidence.notes:
THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT STRUCTURAL DECISION

March's validator was a function pasted into a template. Skipping it was not a decision anyone made; it was what happened by default whenever someone wrote a script without starting from _upgrade-template.mjs. 22 of 43 upgrade scripts did exactly that, and those 22 sections are precisely the 22 that fail the validator today. The replacement must make running the check a property of writing, not a property of the author's diligence.

Concretely, in this codebase, writes reach the eight content tables by exactly four routes:
1. scripts/*.mjs via the shared client in scripts/_db.mjs — 93 of 96 files.
2. scripts/*.mjs, seed/*.mjs, audit/scripts/*.mjs that build their own createClient from .env.local — 3 + 10 + 4 = 17 files, including the September-era audit/scripts/hotfix-packet-0-content.mjs.
3. PUT /api/admin/sections/[id]/[type] via lib/supabase-server.js createServerClient() — auth-checked, content-unchecked.
4. Anything a human runs against Supabase directly (dashboard, psql).

The placement that follows:

(a) GUARD THE CLIENT, NOT THE SCRIPT. Make scripts/_db.mjs export a wrapped client whose .from(table) returns a proxy when `table` is one of the eight CONTENT_TABLES (the list already exists, exported from scripts/snapshot-section.mjs). The proxy intercepts update / upsert / insert. Implementation detail that matters: section_id arrives via a chained .eq('section_id', x) AFTER .update(), so the proxy must defer — collect the payload and the eq filter, and run validation inside then() (Supabase's PostgrestBuilder is a thenable), rejecting the promise with the error list on a BLOCK. For upsert, section_id is in the payload itself. The win is that 93 scripts are converted by editing one file, with no cooperation from any of them: they already do `import { supabase } from './_db.mjs'`.

(b) CLOSE THE SECOND-CLIENT HOLE, THEN KEEP IT CLOSED. Convert the 17 files that build their own client to import from _db.mjs, then add a one-line static guard to the validator run: any createClient( occurrence under scripts/, seed/ or audit/scripts/ outside _db.mjs is a BLOCK. Without this, the guarded client decays the same way validate() did — by someone writing a new file that does not use it.

(c) THE API ROUTE IS NOT OPTIONAL. Write the validator as an isomorphic ESM module (lib/validate/index.mjs) importable from both .mjs scripts and Next server code — the repo already does this successfully with lib/quant/index.mjs, which audit/scripts/quant-check.mjs imports. Then call it in app/api/admin/sections/[id]/[type]/route.js before restoreIds() and return 422 with the structured error list, and render those errors in components/admin/SectionEditor.jsx next to the existing 'Invalid JSON' state. This turns the founder's spot-check into the place where the gate gives feedback, which is the only paid attention available.

(d) A THIN POSTGRES FLOOR. A BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger on the eight tables, holding only the handful of invariants that are cheap in plpgsql and catastrophic to violate — practice (command, marks) against a command_tariffs table, quiz correctIndex in range, required keys present. Do not put 35 checks here; put the three you would never want bypassed by a route nobody has written yet or a paste into the Supabase dashboard.

(e) KEEP THE SWEEP, DEMOTE ITS STATUS. PROTOCOL.md gate step 4 ('Validator green on all 43 sections') should stay, because the write-path guard only sees new writes and 43 sections of existing debt need a repeated full-corpus run. But it is a regression detector, not the gate. PLAN.md line 94 already says why: 'A gate beside the write path is a convention. March had one of those.'

Ordering: (a) and (c) are the gate. (b) is what stops it rotting. (d) is the floor. (e) is the ratchet.

WHAT A VALIDATOR FUNDAMENTALLY CANNOT CHECK — AND THE OVER-TRUST TRAPS

It cannot check truth. The strawberry realExample on `the-market` satisfies all 16 March rules and teaches the law of supply backwards. Every static check in the mechanisable list would pass it.

It cannot check single-answer-ness in a quiz, credit-worthiness in a mark scheme, whether a section teaches a sub-topic rather than merely naming it, whether prose is original rather than paraphrased from a copyrighted source, or whether a 20-mark plan reaches the top level descriptor. Those need reading comprehension plus IAL subject knowledge — that is a model-in-the-loop job, and it is a different packet from this one.

Three specific over-trust traps this codebase is already exposed to:

1. GREEN WILL BE READ AS 'CHECKED'. The March validator was green on 21 of 43 sections, and those 21 carry 246 of the 453 accuracy issues and are all graded C. Whatever the new validator prints on success must say 'no known shape defects' and must print the count of rules that ran, never 'passed'. The report should state the checks it did NOT perform as loudly as the ones it did.

2. MECHANISABLE RULES GET GAMED BY THE GENERATOR. Every static rule becomes a target for the AI authoring the content. 'realExample must contain a capitalised multiword entity' produces plausible fabricated companies. 'guidance mark credits must sum to the tariff' produces padded credits — which is literally the defect the audit found on `meeting-customer-needs` p0. The stricter the checkable surface, the more the uncheckable surface absorbs the failure. This is the strongest argument for PLAN packet 3's BLOCK / DEBT / INFO tiering and for pairing the gate with an adversarial reading pass rather than treating it as a substitute for one.

3. BASELINES BECOME THE NEW NORMAL. package.json already ships `pin-check.mjs --max-broken 15`. A tolerated-failure count with no owner and no expiry stops being a debt marker and becomes the definition of acceptable. Commit each baseline with the ledger ids it covers and the packet that retires it.

And the boundary worth stating plainly for the wider design: a validator measures the artefact. The founder's bar is about the student. Nothing in scripts/, seed/ or lib/ can tell you whether a student who revised here walks into WEC11 prepared. The only asset in this repo that could is past_papers — 75 rows, all 8 units, with mark_scheme_url — used to test students on unseen questions and measure the gap. That is a different mechanism from the gate, and the gate should not be allowed to stand in for it.

Mark tariff not permitted for that command word in that subject (Define 4, Explain 6, Analyse 10, Assess 10 in Economics) - 73 more items fail; combined 173/215 = 80.5%
Marks stated in the question stem disagreeing with the marks field
Points-based mark allocation ('(1 mark)', '3 marks') inside guidance for a levels-marked item of 8 marks or more - 66 live items
MCQ answer-key distribution skew, per section and corpus-wide (chi-square or max-share threshold): 39/43 sections >=50% one index; corpus 64% option B
Correct option is the longest option at above-chance rate (39/43 sections at >=50%)
Duplicate or near-duplicate options inside one MCQ (financial-planning quiz[3])
Duplicate or near-duplicate stems within a section's bank, and cross-section stem collisions
Leaked authoring notes and placeholders in explanations (TODO, FIXME, 'actually', trailing ellipsis mid-sentence)
Currency/unit sanity in stems: same symbol on both sides of an exchange-rate pair, percentages that do not sum, arithmetic in a stem that contradicts the keyed option (extract numerals, recompute)
quizIndices / practiceIndices out of range, and the marks-sort identity bug (index resolved against a sorted array vs the raw array)
Fill-in hint leakage: hint shares a prefix with its answer or matches its exact length (138/141 and 80/141 live)
Fill-in word bank containing only correct answers (no distractors) - solvable by elimination
Reorder recall not derived from a body flow of >=3 steps or an extras.chains entry (the structural rule the pedagogy critique proposes); reorder with <=3 items

Spec-term presence scan: required spec sub-bullet terms absent from a section, and off-spec terms present (grep against audit/raw/econ_spec.txt and bus_spec.txt - the method that produced the spec-gap list)
Section meta.number not matching an official spec heading for its unit code

Command-word glossary and term glossary consistency: every word in command_words must exist for that subject, every IAL command word must be present ('Examine' is missing), subject_id must not be null
UK-domestic token list (NHS, CMA, Bank of England, ONS, HS2, Ofsted) in content aimed at an international cohort
Stable item ids present on every quiz/practice/recall object before any content write (spaced-repetition state is keyed to array position)
Coverage accounting itself: items reviewed must equal items in the section, so a reviewer that skips items fails the gate arithmetically
Verbatim-quote verification: re-find every quote a reviewer cites in the source JSON; a quote that does not exist voids the finding (2 of 88 verdicts already caught mis-cited line numbers)
judgementOnly: Is a named real-world example factually true - entity, date, number, and whether the event is an instance of the concept (eBay/Skype 2009 sold to Microsoft; Under Armour's positioning; post-Brexit fisheries tariff access; Scottish salmon as trade diversion)
Does an example illustrate the mechanism it claims, or has it been stylised to fit (UK strawberries presented as movement along the supply curve when it is a seasonal shift)
Conceptual reversals that read fluently: consumption vs investment volatility, welfare loss as MSC-MPC area from 0 to Qm, P>ATC as the short-run supply condition, transfer payments inside G
Terminology muddles where both terms are real: response bias vs question bias, demerger vs divestment, deadweight loss vs the spec's 'welfare loss areas'
Whether a flow/chain is genuinely causal or three unrelated facts rendered as arrows
Whether a reorder sequence has a defensible unique order, or is a list, a taxonomy, or contains a meta-item ('not-orderable' 18, 'weak-or-arbitrary' 48 of 272)
Whether a recall item is worth recalling at all ('trivial' 66 of 272) - a judgement about what the exam rewards
Cross-item contradiction: two questions in the same bank keying opposite answers on one concept (market-failure quiz[5] vs quiz[18])
Whether an item belongs to this spec point or another unit (Laffer curve in 3.3.5; gearing in WBS12 2.3; theory-of-the-firm in a WEC11 supply bank)
Whether a model answer would actually reach Level 4 under the levels grid, and whether guidance teaches the right marking model
Whether examMatters accurately states what the mark scheme awards
Difficulty and stimulus realism: whether a 20-marker is answerable without the case-study extract a real paper supplies

Whether the section as a whole would leave a student prepared - the question no single-item check can answer

findings: MEASURED DISAGREEMENT RATE (code review only): audit/raw/code-verdicts.json holds 88 adversarial verdicts, one per skeptic agent (88 distinct agentIds). 6 of 88 (6.8%) returned refuted=true. Reading all six: every one confirms the mechanical claim as literally true and refutes only the claimed student impact ('Code claim verified as literally true...', 'Mechanics confirmed, conclusion not'). All six were re-graded to correctedSeverity 'low'. Zero findings were killed on fact. The skeptic pass is a severity calibrator, not a fact-checker.

SEVERITY IS WHERE AI REVIEWERS ARE UNRELIABLE, NOT FACTS: corrected severities across the 88 verdicts are 0 critical / 21 high / 51 medium / 16 low, drawn from a finding pool (audit/raw/code-findings-flat.json, 117 items) graded 5 critical / 35 high / 53 medium / 24 low. No finding retained 'critical' after verification. 25 of 88 verdict texts contain 'inflat*', 15 contain 'overstat*', 4 'exaggerat*'.

INDEPENDENT REVIEWERS CONVERGE ON EXISTENCE, NOT ON PRIORITY: clustering the 117 code findings by file basename + line within +/-8 (my heuristic, stated as such) gives 85 distinct defect clusters. 19 were found by more than one of the 9 lens briefs; 16 of those 19 (84%) carry a severity disagreement between the reviewers who found them (e.g. app/api/learn-mode/progress route.js:48 graded 'high' by one lens and 'medium' by another; route.js:57-60 'medium' vs 'low').

ONE REVIEWER SEES ABOUT A THIRD OF WHAT NINE SEE: 72 of 117 code findings (62%) sit in clusters touched by exactly one lens. Cluster frequency across lenses is {1 lens: 66, 2: 16, 3: 2, 4: 1}; a Chao1 capture-recapture estimate on that distribution is ~221 detectable defects against 85 observed, i.e. an upper bound of ~62% missed by the nine-reviewer panel. Caveat: the briefs were deliberately partitioned by surface, which violates Chao1's homogeneity assumption and inflates the estimate; treat it as directional.

SAME BRIEF, DIFFERENT FINDINGS: audit/raw/code-lenses.json contains two separate agents both labelled lens 'shell-onboarding-retention' (15 and 14 findings). Clustered together they share only 2 defects out of 23 in the union (Jaccard 0.087), and on those 2 they agree on severity once. Redundancy on an identical brief buys very little; consensus/majority-vote is therefore not a usable pass test.

ITEM-LOCAL RULE CHECKS ARE NEAR-PERFECT WHEN THE RULE IS IN THE BRIEF: I re-ran the IAL command-word/tariff table (audit/README.md) over all 215 live practice items in audit/content-sections/*.json. 173 of 215 (80.5%) fail a pure table lookup (92 Economics, 81 Business). Matching each failure against audit/raw/content-audits.json practiceIssues by index, the September reviewers flagged 171 of 173 (98.8%). Only two were missed (influences-business-decisions #3, managing-change #3).

DISTRIBUTIONAL DEFECTS ARE WHERE AI REVIEW FAILS: 39 of 43 sections have >=50% of MCQ answer keys on a single option index. The section audits mention answer-key skew in only 21 of those 39 (54% recall). Missed sections include external-influences (21/25 on index 1), government-intervention (21/25), managing-finance (19/25), macroeconomic-objectives-policies (19/25). A three-line static check catches 39/39.

THE CORPUS-WIDE VERSION OF THAT DEFECT APPEARS NOWHERE IN THE AUDIT: across all 769 live MCQs the key distribution is A 37, B 492, C 219, D 21. Always answering B scores 64.0% platform-wide without reading anything. No section reviewer could see this because each saw one section; no artefact in audit/raw states it.

SHARED CROSS-SECTION ASSETS WERE NEVER REVIEWED: 0 of 43 section audits mention the glossary (audit/raw/glossary_terms.json, 372 live terms). audit/raw/command_words.json (18 live rows shown to students) was never audited either, and is wrong: subject_id is null on all 18 rows, 'Examine' (the real IAL Economics 8-mark command) is absent, and 10 non-IAL words are present (State, Identify, Outline, Describe, Distinguish, Compare, Justify, Suggest, To what extent, Consider). Section-scoped review structurally cannot see this.

WHOLE ARTEFACT CLASSES WERE UNDER-SAMPLED: live inventory across the 43 snapshots is 844 flashcards, 769 quiz, 413 subsections (each with realExample + misconception + examMatters), 341 flows, 272 recalls, 215 practice, 202 notes, 188 common_mistakes, 306 extras (chains + evaluation), 81 diagrams. Classifying the 453 accuracyIssues by the artefact named in their 'location' field: 7 cite a flashcard, 5 notes, 4 common_mistakes, 1 extras, 27 diagrams, 13 quiz, 106 content, 268 unlabelled prose. Flashcards got 7 findings across 844 items.

CENSUS COVERAGE IS ACHIEVABLE WHEN ITEMS ARE ENUMERATED: the reviewers judged 272 of 272 live recall widgets (recallAudit entries exactly equal the 272 recalls I counted in the snapshots) with verdicts trivial 66, genuine-sequence 64, hint-leaks-answer 51, weak-or-arbitrary-sequence 48, not-orderable 18, ambiguous-answers 14, fine 11 - only 75 of 272 (27.6%) sound. practiceIssues (224) likewise exceed the 215 practice items. Where items were enumerable, coverage was complete.

WHERE ITEMS WERE NOT ENUMERATED, OUTPUT LOOKS QUOTA-SHAPED: accuracyIssues per section run 6-15 (median 10, stdev 2.15) regardless of section size, while quizIssues correlate with bank size at r=0.70 (769 items, 398 issues). Prose accuracy review was a fixed-effort sample, not a census - so '453 accuracy issues' is a floor, not a count.

THE HOLISTIC GRADE CARRIES NO INFORMATION AND MUST NOT BE THE PASS CONDITION: 38 sections graded C, 5 graded D, none A or B. Mean total issues C 42.4 vs D 41.0; mean high+critical issues 5.0 vs 5.0. business-growth has 8 high-severity issues and scored C; role-state-macroeconomy has 2 and scored D. The same reviewer's item-level findings do not predict its own letter.

CONTENT FINDINGS HAVE NEVER BEEN ADVERSARIALLY VERIFIED: all 88 verdicts cite .jsx/.js/.css/.sql files; 0 cite content-sections, accuracyIssues or quizIssues. The 6.8% disagreement rate is measured on code review only. The 1,170 content work items - the part that determines exam preparedness - carry a single unverified reviewer's opinion each.

THE SIX CRITICAL FACTUAL ERRORS ARE REAL AND WERE CAUGHT: critical-severity content items are exactly 6 accuracy + 8 quiz + 4 practice (matching PLAN.md's day-0 list of '6 false examples, 8 wrongly keyed quiz items, 4 off-topic practice items'), spread over 15 sections. Examples: eBay 'demerged Skype in 2009, selling it to Microsoft' (wrong buyer, wrong year, wrong concept); consumption described as 'the largest and most volatile component of AD' contradicting three other places in the same section; transfer payments taught as part of G against the section's own quiz[13]; UK strawberry supply example that inverts the law of supply.

THREE OF THOSE CRITICALS ARE ALSO CATCHABLE WITH NO MODEL AT ALL - I reproduced them with ~200 lines of Python over the snapshots: financial-planning quiz[3] has two identical '£500' options with only one keyed correct; external-influences quiz[15] reads '$1 = $1.30 to $1 = $1.40' (same symbol both sides); the-market quiz[18] explanation contains a leaked authoring note ('Revenue rises from $20,000 to $20,000... actually revenue = 500x40=20,000 vs 400x5...').

MECHANICAL RULES OVER-FLAG RELATIVE TO JUDGEMENT, SO THEY MUST FEED REVIEWERS, NOT GATE ALONE: 138 of 141 fill-in recalls have hints that reveal the answer's first letter(s) and 80 also match the answer's exact length, yet the reviewers assigned 'hint-leaks-answer' to only 51 of 272 recalls - they flagged it only where the leak actually made the item answerable without recall. Exact rules (tariff table, duplicate options) can gate; heuristics cannot.

THE MARCH VALIDATOR CHECKED NOTHING THAT MATTERS: validate() in scripts/_upgrade-template.mjs checks field presence, keyIdea <=180 chars, takeaway <=100 chars, no bold in keyIdea, >=3 takeaway items, flow steps 2-4, resultType in {good,bad,neutral}, and duplicate subsection ids. It never sees quiz, practice, marks, command words, answer keys or recalls - the arrays where every critical defect lives.

THE NON-EXPERT HUMAN SPOT-CHECK IS UNRELIABLE ON MECHANISM AND RELIABLE ON SYMPTOM: audit/raw/research-founder-report-factcheck.md adjudicates the founder's own 10 claims - 6 FALSE (a,b,c,e,h,j), 2 PARTLY (g,i), 1 true-but-miscounted (f), 1 unverifiable (d) - and its summary is that roughly a third is grounded observation. The same document lists 10 real problems he missed. Founder attention should be spent on 'does this look like the exam / is this claim true', never on mechanism adjudication.

AI REVIEW OF AI PLANNING ALSO SURFACES REAL GAPS: audit/raw/plan-coverage-check.json records 10 coverage agents over 1,765 plan items returning 138 uncovered and 69 weakly covered, plus 4 independent critiques returning 3 'needs-restructure' and 1 'sound-with-changes'. Multi-agent critique of a plan behaves like multi-lens review of code: high yield, low overlap.
evidence.notes:
VERDICT ON THE CORE QUESTION. AI review can substitute for an examiner on detection of item-local, rule-checkable and factual defects - measured 98.8% recall (171/173) on the tariff class, a complete 272/272 census on recalls, and all 18 criticals found. It cannot substitute on prioritisation (6/88 skeptic refutations were all severity overturns, no critical survived verification), on distributional defects (54% recall, 21/39 sections, on answer-key skew), on anything outside a section's own JSON (0/43 audits touched the 372-term glossary or the 18-row command-word table), or on the terminal question of whether a student is exam-ready. So the gate is not 'AI instead of an examiner'; it is 'a static gate that makes the examiner's rule-following job unnecessary, plus AI reviewers spending their whole budget on the judgement residue, plus an adversary who grades severity, plus 10 minutes of founder attention aimed only at symptoms'.

PROPOSED REVIEW PROTOCOL.

Stage 0 - static gate, no model call, runs before any reviewer sees the section, no override. Every rule in the 'mechanisable' list. Today it fails 173/215 practice items and 39/43 sections, which is the measure of how much reviewer attention it buys back. Two rules are hard blocks with no judgement (tariff table, duplicate options); the heuristics (hint leakage, longest-key, UK tokens) emit a worklist that is handed to Stage 1 rather than failing the build, because the mechanical rule over-flags: 138/141 hint leaks by rule vs 51/272 by judgement.

Stage 1 - three reviewers, three distinct briefs, same section, no shared context, each producing an enumerated census with a count that must equal the section's item count. Three and not two because same-brief duplication overlapped at Jaccard 0.087; distinct briefs partition the surface far better than redundancy.
R1 EXAMINER. Given: the spec extract for that spec point, the canonical tariff table, one real mark scheme PDF for that unit from past_papers, the section JSON. Asked: for every practice item, what level would this model answer reach and why; for every examMatters claim, does the mark scheme award that; which spec sub-bullets are absent. Output is per-item, with the mark-scheme clause quoted.
R2 FACT-CHECKER. Given: the section JSON only, no spec, no other reviewer. Asked: every realExample (entity, date, figure, and whether it instantiates the concept), every definition, every flow chain's causality, every quiz explanation's internal arithmetic. Must quote the exact sentence and state the correct fact with a source. This is the brief that found eBay/Skype, Under Armour, the fisheries claim and the strawberry inversion.
R3 EXPLOITER. Given: only what a student sees, with the prose withheld. Asked to answer every quiz, recall and fill-in item without reading the teaching content, and report its score. Its score is the finding. This is the only brief that catches distributional and surface-cue defects, the exact class the September review missed 46% of; today it would score 64% platform-wide by answering B.
Never ask any reviewer for 'the top N issues'. The quota artefact is visible in the data: accuracy issues cluster at 6-15 per section (stdev 2.15) independent of section size, while enumerated classes reached 100% coverage.

Stage 2 - adversary, one per surviving finding, refute mandate, told the finding is probably wrong, given the section, the spec and the finding but not the reviewer's reasoning. Must return refuted true/false plus correctedSeverity with verbatim evidence. Measured behaviour: 6 refutations, 10+ explicit severity corrections, 0 criticals surviving, 2 catches of mis-cited line numbers. It is a calibrator - do not expect it to find new facts.

Stage 3 - pass condition. Union of findings, never intersection: consensus is unavailable (Jaccard 0.087) and demanding it would discard 62% of what a panel finds. A section ships only when all of: (1) Stage 0 green; (2) reviewed-item count equals section item count for all three reviewers; (3) zero findings open at corrected severity critical or high; (4) R3's blind score is within 10 points of chance; (5) every finding's verbatim quote re-found in the file; (6) founder sample clears - one practice item, one realExample, and the single highest-severity finding, answered only as 'does this look like the exam' / 'is this claim true'. The letter grade is banned from the pass condition: C mean 42.4 issues vs D mean 41.0, and identical mean high+critical counts (5.0 vs 5.0), so the holistic judgement did not track the same reviewer's own items.

ANTI-RUBBER-STAMPING, ranked by how much evidence stands behind each. Strong: census-with-count instead of top-N (enumerated classes hit 100%, sampled prose hit a quota); verbatim-quote re-verification (already caught 2/88 mis-citations); reviewer isolation and an adversary that never sees the builder's conversation (already mandated in PROTOCOL.md for Verify A); severity set by the adversary, not the finder. Untested: seeded canaries - inject 3 known defects per section drawn from the 18 confirmed criticals held out as a bank (one wrong tariff, one false named-entity fact, one mis-keyed MCQ), void any reviewer that misses one, and track per-brief canary recall over time so a degrading brief can be retired. I have no measurement that canaries work here; it is the one component of this design proposed on reasoning rather than evidence, and it should be validated on the first five sections before being trusted.

HONEST LIMITS. The 6.8% disagreement rate is measured on code review only - 88/88 verdicts cite code files, 0 cite content - so no content finding in this repo has ever been second-opinioned, and the reliability figures should be read as an optimistic transfer to content. Capture-recapture on the nine-brief code panel puts observed defects at 85 against an estimated ~221, an upper bound on the miss rate since the briefs were partitioned. Whole artefact classes remain effectively unreviewed (844 flashcards drew 7 findings, 306 extras drew 1). And the bar the founder set - a student as well prepared as one who used expert material - is not decidable by any review protocol: it is decided by past-paper performance. The one instrument that could measure it is already in the database (75 real papers with mark schemes), and the honest framing is that this gate makes content defensible, while only student marks on those papers make it verified.

designs.name: The Unrepresentable Gate
designs.premise: The paid examiner's real job was catching format and coverage defects — 55% of the failures sit in five structural classes and 65% are reachable by code with no money and no judgement — so spend the whole mechanisation budget on making those defects impossible to author rather than merely possible to detect, and buy back every agent-minute and all eight of the founder's minutes for the 35% that is actual economics.

stages.stage: S0 — Fixture build (one-time, before packet 14; becomes packet 3's real deliverable)
stages.input: audit/raw/econ_spec.txt, bus_spec.txt, research-ial-spec-coverage.md lines 113-154, the 72 mark-scheme PDFs and 14 question papers behind past_papers (75 rows, 86 URLs), audit/content-sections/*.json as the replay corpus
stages.passCondition: `node audit/scripts/fixture-check.mjs` exits 0, asserting all of: (a) every row of audit/fixtures/tariffs.json carries subject, unit, command, marks, marking_mode, ao_split, grid count and band boundaries, n_sightings >= 2, and a past_papers id plus question number that resolves; (b) the table reproduces the measured census exactly — Business Assess-12 n=25, Economics Evaluate-20 n=45, point-mark credit tokens 1K=226 / 1AN=240 / 1AP=39, Economics two grids / Business one; (c) fixtures/command_words.json contains exactly the 8 Economics and 8 Business IAL commands, zero words with 0 corpus sightings (kills State, Identify, Outline, Describe, Distinguish, Compare, Justify, Suggest, Consider) and both Examine and Construct present; (d) replaying the table over the 43 t=0 snapshots flags exactly 173 of 215 practice items and 123 of 215 on the (command, marks) rule alone — a different number means the parser is still lossy and the fixture must not ship. Also emitted here: fixtures/spec-bullets.json (bullet -> required keywords), fixtures/offspec-denylist.json, fixtures/uk-tokens.json.
stages.cost: one-time: 1 authoring agent + 1 verifier agent; 0 founder minutes

stages.stage: S1 — Schema contract: make the five structural classes unrepresentable (one-time, extends packets 2 and 7)
stages.input: the eight content tables, fixtures from S0, packet 7's widget decisions, the 43 t=0 snapshots
stages.passCondition: `node audit/scripts/schema-replay.mjs` exits 0, asserting that loading all 43 t=0 snapshots under the new schema rejects exactly the known-bad populations and prints each count: 769 authored correctIndex values (the field no longer exists — an author sets correct:true on one option and a deterministic balanced allocator assigns positions, so per-section max key share is capped at 30% by construction), 141 fill-in hint fields (field deleted; a distractor bank replaces it), 131 stored `shuffled` arrays (render-time shuffle only), 173 typed (command, marks) pairs (practice items carry shape_id FK into fixtures/tariffs.json; command, marks, ao_split, marking_mode and band boundaries are derived, never typed), 799 orphan items (648 quiz + 151 practice — every assessment item must carry the block_id that owns it, so wiring is authored, not inferred), and every item missing spec_bullet_id. Counts must match exactly; a mismatch means the schema is looser than claimed.
stages.cost: one-time: 1 authoring agent + 1 verifier agent; 0 founder minutes

stages.stage: S2 — Write-path validator, blocking, no override
stages.who: static check (0 model calls), inside lib/validate/index.mjs
stages.input: the section payload across all eight tables at the moment of write, plus audit/fixtures/*
stages.passCondition: `node audit/scripts/validate-section.mjs <slug> --strict` exits 0 with zero BLOCK findings, and `node audit/scripts/writepath-check.mjs` exits 0 asserting the validator is unbypassable: zero `createClient(` occurrences under scripts/, seed/ or audit/scripts/ outside _db.mjs (17 files must be converted first), scripts/_db.mjs exports a proxy that validates inside then() for the eight CONTENT_TABLES, and app/api/admin/sections/[id]/[type]/route.js imports the same module and returns 422 before restoreIds(). ~40 rules, tiered: BLOCK (tariff/shape lookup, grid bands, ao_split sums to marks, levels item has a non-empty stimulus, spec_bullet resolves, off-spec denylist, duplicate options, unsourced 'Examiners reward/expect/penalise' sentence, n-gram overlap vs the 86 extracted PDFs above threshold, currency mixing, UK-token denylist, dangling diagramRef, zero-diagram or zero-recall section, no Calculate item in the set); DEBT (heuristics that over-flag — longest-correct-option, glossary-term-not-taught, near-duplicate stem — which emit a worklist handed to S4, never a build failure); INFO. Every DEBT item must carry a ledger id and the packet number that retires it, or the run fails.
stages.cost: 0 agents, 0 founder minutes; runs in milliseconds on every write

stages.stage: S3 — Blind exploiter (the number that measures the student, not the artefact)
stages.input: only what a student sees with the teaching prose withheld: quiz stems and options, practice stems, recall widgets, flashcard fronts. No body text, no explanations, no keys, no spec.
stages.passCondition: Agent returns JSON; a script checks three numbers. MCQ score <= 35% (4-option chance 25% + 10pp; today the corpus scores 64% by always answering B and 70% by always picking the longest option), <= 1 recall widget solved without the prose, and no single option index holds more than 35% of that section's keys. Any number over threshold fails the section back to S2 — this is the only stage that measures the property the founder actually cares about and it costs one agent.

stages.stage: S4 — Judgement panel: three isolated briefs, census-counted, canaries pre-injected
stages.who: review agents (3, Fable for R1/R2 on packet 14, Opus thereafter)
stages.input: R1 EXAMINER: the spec extract for the section's bullets, fixtures/tariffs.json, one real mark scheme PDF for that unit from past_papers, the section JSON. R2 FACT-CHECKER: the section JSON only — no spec, no other reviewer, web search allowed. R3 COHERENCE: all eight tables for the section plus glossary_terms.json and command_words.json, asked only for cross-surface contradiction and term-first-use ordering. Each copy carries three seeded canaries from a held-out bank. No reviewer sees another's output or the builder's conversation.
stages.passCondition: Arithmetic, not judgement: for each brief, reviewed_item_count == the section's count in audit/raw/section-index.json for the artefact classes that brief owns (a reviewer that skips items fails the gate by subtraction — this is what turned recall review into a 272/272 census while prose review stalled at a 6-15 quota); every finding's `quote` field re-found verbatim in the section JSON by script (already caught 2 of 88 mis-citations on the code side); every finding written to audit/ledger.json as C-<section>-<kind>-<nn>. Findings are unioned, never intersected — same-brief redundancy overlapped at Jaccard 0.087, so consensus would discard most of what a panel finds. The words 'top N issues' must not appear in any brief.

stages.stage: S5 — Canary adjudication (liveness check on the panel itself)
stages.who: static check against the canary manifest
stages.input: the union of S4 findings plus the manifest of the three defects injected into each reviewer's copy — one invalid tariff (R1's class), one false named-entity fact modelled on the eBay/Skype or Tesla-gigafactory criticals (R2's class), one mis-keyed MCQ with two defensible options (R1/R3)
stages.passCondition: All 3 canaries appear in the union, each attributed to the brief that owns its class. A miss voids that brief's entire output for this section and the brief re-runs once with a fresh agent; two consecutive misses retires the brief, recorded in DECISIONS.md. Per-brief canary recall is appended to PROGRESS.md every section so a degrading brief is visible as a trend rather than as a surprise at section 40.
