stages.cost: 0 agents, 0 founder minutes (re-run costs 1 agent when it fires)

stages.stage: S6 — Adversary / severity calibrator
stages.who: review agent (1 per surviving finding, Sonnet)
stages.input: the finding, the section, the spec — and explicitly NOT the reviewer's reasoning; told the finding is probably wrong and given a refute mandate
stages.passCondition: verdict count == finding count; every verdict carries refuted true/false, correctedSeverity and verbatim evidence; zero findings remain open at corrected severity critical or high. Expect it to behave as it did on code: 6.8% refutations, all of them severity overturns, zero facts killed. It is a calibrator, not a second fact-checker — do not credit it with finding anything new.
stages.cost: roughly 10-25 agents per section, one per finding; 0 founder minutes

stages.stage: S7 — Founder symptom check (the only human minutes in the design)
stages.input: exactly four things on one screen, in a fixed form, with mechanism hidden: (1) one practice item rendered as it would appear on a paper, beside the anchor's paper code, session and question number; (2) the three realExamples R2 marked verified-true, one sentence each; (3) the single highest corrected-severity open finding, in one sentence; (4) the S3 blind-exploiter score as one number against 25%.
stages.passCondition: Three recorded answers via `node audit/scripts/ledger.mjs founder <slug> --paper yes|no --examples yes|no --finding ship|hold`. The questions are only ever 'would this look at home on a WEC11 paper', 'do you believe these three claims', 'ship or hold'. Any 'no' or 'hold' reopens the section at S2. He is never asked to adjudicate mechanism — the founder factcheck document puts roughly a third of his own mechanism claims as grounded, and the same document lists ten real problems he missed; he is reliable on symptom and unreliable on cause, and the form must not let him be asked the wrong kind of question.
stages.cost: 8 founder minutes per section (45 minutes once, for packet 14, because it sets the template for 42 more)

stages.stage: S8 — Exam-truth probe (every fifth section, i.e. at the existing ship checkpoints)
stages.who: review agents (3: treatment, control, blind marker)
stages.input: real past-paper questions for that unit from the 14 question papers that have a matching mark scheme (11 complete slots), the real mark scheme, and the platform content shipped so far
stages.passCondition: Treatment agent answers using only platform content as its knowledge base; control answers with the platform content withheld; a third agent marks both blind against the real mark scheme grid. Pass is (treatment - control) >= 0 at the first checkpoint and non-decreasing at every later one; a negative delta is a content regression and blocks the ship. Only the delta is read, never the absolute score. This is the one instrument in the repo that speaks to the founder's actual bar, and it is deliberately outside the per-section gate so nobody mistakes it for one.
stages.cost: 3 agents per five sections; 0 founder minutes

stages.stage: S9 — Packet gate (existing PROTOCOL.md lifecycle, unchanged)
stages.who: static check + verifier agents already defined
stages.input: the packet's diff, the ledger, the dev server at 390px
stages.passCondition: `npm run build` green; `node audit/scripts/ledger.mjs unverified <n>` exits 0; validate-section --strict green on all 43 sections (the corpus sweep, which is a regression detector and must never be described as the gate); Verify A (packet-verifier, read-only, fresh context, file:line evidence per claimed id) and Verify B (student-walkthrough at 390px) attached to NEXT.md; PROGRESS row updated with the S3 score, the S5 canary result and the S8 delta if the checkpoint fell here; committed with packet-<n>: and pushed.

catches: The five structural classes that are 1,105 of 2,013 failures (54.9%) stop being detectable and become unauthorable. Wrong exam shape (246) dies because command, marks, ao_split, marking mode and band boundaries are derived from a shape_id FK, not typed. MCQ construction skew (201) dies because correctIndex is not an authored field — a balanced allocator assigns positions, capping per-section key share at 30% by construction. Fill-in hint leakage (141 of 141 live, 130 judged failures) dies because the hint field is deleted. Reorder permutation reuse (99 of 131 on two permutations) dies because shuffle moves to render time and the stored array is gone. Wiring orphans (648 quiz + 151 practice) die because block_id is mandatory on every assessment item.

Everything in the pure-static tier that survives the schema change: 244 unsourced 'Examiners reward/penalise' sentences now need a mark-scheme citation or the write is refused; 26 sections carrying UK-only tokens and 16 mixing currencies; 20 zero-diagram and 24 zero-recall sections; 3 dangling diagramRefs; 43 of 43 sections with no Calculate item; 62 levels-marked items with no stimulus; the 0 of 215 items that currently satisfy both a real tariff and a real stimulus.

The two reference-data bugs that caused March and would have been inherited by any naive gate: nine command words that exist in neither IAL taxonomy, and two real ones missing. S0 rebuilds the table from 72 mark schemes with per-row sighting counts and a resolvable paper citation, and refuses to ship unless the replay flags exactly 173 of 215 live practice items.

The corpus-wide distributional defect that no per-section reviewer could see — 64% of all 769 MCQs keyed to B, 70% keyed to the longest option, 39 of 43 sections skewed ≥50% on one index. I reproduced this myself against the snapshots; it is a three-line check, and the balanced allocator makes it structurally impossible going forward rather than merely reported.

Rubber-stamping by reviewers, to the extent evidence supports any method: census-with-count instead of top-N (the class that reached 272/272 coverage versus prose review's 6-15-per-section quota, stdev 2.15, independent of section size), verbatim-quote re-verification by script, reviewer isolation, severity set by an adversary who never sees the finder's reasoning, and canaries with a retirement rule.

The one property that is about the student rather than the artefact: S3's blind score. A section where the assessment can be beaten without the teaching cannot ship, and the threshold is a number a session checks without judgement.

Copyright, on the narrow axis it can be checked: n-gram overlap of every authored stem, stimulus and rubric against the extracted text of all 86 PDFs, plus a required different scenario domain, which blocks the rename-the-company paraphrase that is the obvious failure mode of anchor-based authoring.
misses: It does not catch wrong economics, and that is 290 failures (classes 5 and 15, 14.4%) including the worst student-facing outcome in the corpus. The Toyota JIT chip-shortage story is inverted, the Tesla gigafactory financing is invented, the strawberry example teaches the law of supply backwards, and every one of these satisfies every structural rule I have written. My whole answer to this class is R2, a single fact-checking agent with a knowledge cutoff, no examiner training, and an error rate that has never been measured on content — all 88 adversarial verdicts in this repo cite code files and zero cite content. I am proposing as the examiner's replacement the same reviewer role whose reliability is unmeasured, and the canaries are the only thing standing between that and a rubber stamp.

Canaries are the load-bearing liveness check and they are the one component in this design proposed on reasoning rather than evidence. If seeded defects turn out to be trivially distinguishable from organic ones — a plausible failure, since an injected false fact may read differently from an authored one — then a degrading brief passes its canary and misses everything real, and nobody finds out for 42 sections. Validate canaries on the first five sections and be willing to conclude they do not work.

Making defects unrepresentable pushes the failure into the uncheckable surface rather than eliminating it. An authoring agent that cannot pick a wrong tariff will write a correctly-tariffed, correctly-banded, correctly-stimulated question that no examiner would set — and it will do so more fluently than before, because every mechanical signal now reads green. The stricter the checkable surface, the more confidently wrong the uncheckable one looks. This is the central risk of the design and I do not have a mitigation beyond S4 and eight founder minutes.

Three briefs is a guess. Capture-recapture on the nine-brief code panel put observed defects at 85 against an estimated ~221, an upper bound of ~62% missed by nine reviewers; 62% of code findings sat in clusters touched by exactly one lens. I chose three because same-brief duplication overlapped at Jaccard 0.087, which argues that distinct briefs beat redundancy — it does not argue that three is enough, and I have no evidence that it is.

The exam-truth probe measures whether a language model can answer a real past-paper question from the platform's content. That is not the founder's bar. A model brings pretraining knowledge of IAL Economics that no student has; the treatment-minus-control design reduces the confound but cannot remove it, and the probe is structurally blind to pedagogical insufficiency — content that is technically complete and unlearnable by a 17-year-old scores well. The only honest measure of the founder's bar is student marks on unseen past papers, which this design does not produce.

Calibrating any check against audit/raw/content-audits.json measures agreement with one unverified reviewer, not with an examiner. If that reviewer was systematically wrong about a class — and 6 of 88 code verdicts overturned severity while confirming mechanics, so systematic miscalibration is demonstrated in the adjacent corpus — the gate inherits the error and reports green with a confident number attached.

The founder's eight minutes are a smoke alarm, not a gate. Restricting him to symptom questions raises his hit rate, but a well-formed false example is exactly what he will wave through: it will be fluent, named, dated and plausible, which is the shape of every one of the six critical accuracy failures. If R2 misses a fabricated case study, S7 will miss it too, and it ships.

Nothing here establishes originality against sources the founder does not hold. The n-gram check compares against 86 Pearson PDFs; a passage paraphrased from a textbook, a competitor's revision site or a marking guide outside that corpus is undetectable by any check in this design.

A per-section gate is structurally blind to new corpus-wide properties. I have hard-coded away the one we know about (answer-position skew) by construction, but the next one — some cross-section uniformity nobody has thought to look for — will be invisible for the same reason the September panel missed this one: every reviewer saw one section, and no artefact in the audit stated the platform-wide number.

Baselines will rot. package.json already ships pin-check --max-broken 15, a tolerated-failure count with no owner and no expiry. My DEBT tier will do the same thing unless every DEBT item carries a ledger id and a retiring packet — which I have made a pass condition, and which will be the first rule quietly relaxed at section 20 when a packet is running long.
designs.firstThingToBuild: audit/scripts/build-fixtures.mjs and its output audit/fixtures/tariffs.json — the observed-corpus tariff table, one row per (subject, unit, command, marks) with marking_mode, ao_split, grid count, band boundaries, n_sightings and a resolvable past_papers id plus question number, parsed from all 72 mark schemes and reconciled until the parser recovers items from all 72 files rather than the 58 it manages today. Ship it with audit/scripts/fixture-check.mjs, which refuses the table unless it reproduces the census (Business Assess-12 n=25, Economics Evaluate-20 n=45, credit tokens 1K=226 / 1AN=240 / 1AP=39) and flags exactly 173 of 215 live practice items when replayed over the 43 t=0 snapshots — so the calibration harness and the golden-set replay come free in the same build. Build this first because every high-yield check reads it, because the table it replaces (audit/raw/command_words.json) contains nine command words with zero sightings across 72 real papers and is missing Examine and Construct, and because a gate built on the app's own contaminated vocabulary reproduces the March bug with a green light on top. Separately and today, not as part of the gate: the past-papers Supabase bucket is world-readable and is currently redistributing 86 Pearson-copyright PDFs to anyone with the URL — make it private and have the pipeline read it with the service key.

designs.name: The Prosecution Gate
designs.premise: A section ships not because anyone approved it but because a sequence of independent attackers — a static gate that cannot be skipped, four reviewers with deliberately conflicting briefs, a skeptic per finding, and a proxy student who sits a real past-paper question — all failed to break it, and because each of those attackers was itself scored against defects we secretly planted, so the gate's own error rate is a measured number rather than a hope.

stages.stage: S1 — Arraignment: static gate inside the write path (not beside it)
stages.input: The authored section JSON at the moment it is written. Enforced in two places so it cannot be bypassed: a proxy on the shared client in scripts/_db.mjs that intercepts insert/update/upsert for the eight CONTENT_TABLES (93 of 96 scripts converted by editing one file), and lib/validate/index.mjs called from PUT /api/admin/sections/[id]/[type] before restoreIds(), returning 422 into the SectionEditor UI. Reads a fingerprinted reference bundle: the corrected IAL command/tariff table, the spec-bullet keyword map, the off-spec denylist, the reviewed glossary.
stages.passCondition: `npm run gate -- --section <slug>` exits 0 on the BLOCK tier. Every DEBT-tier item carries a ledger id and a target packet number (a tolerated count with no owner is itself a BLOCK). sha256 of each file in audit/ref/ equals the value recorded in PROTOCOL.md — the gate refuses to run against unfingerprinted reference data, because the current command_words.json contains nine words that exist in neither IAL taxonomy. No override flag exists in the code. Success prints 'no known shape defects, N rules ran' and the list of classes it did NOT check; it never prints 'passed'.
stages.cost: 0 agents, ~2s CPU, 0 founder minutes. Runs during authoring, so the author iterates against it for free.

stages.stage: S2 — Anchor and copyright attestation
stages.input: Every practice item's anchor block (anchor_paper_id, anchor_question, provenance, command, marks, marking_mode, ao_split, level_grids, ceilings, qs_codes) plus the past_papers table (75 rows, 86 resolving PDFs) and the pdftotext extraction of all 86 PDFs held locally, never served.
stages.passCondition: 100% of practice items resolve anchor_paper_id to a past_papers row; each (subject, unit, command, marks, marking_mode, grid shape, band boundaries) tuple matches one observed at least twice in the 72 mark schemes (this alone rejects 173 of the 215 live items); every levels-marked item carries a non-empty authored stimulus (62 live items currently fail); point-marked model answers carry (1K)/(1AP)/(1AN)/(1EV) tokens whose counts equal the declared ao_split; max 7-gram overlap against the extracted corpus below threshold with zero 12-gram matches; scenario_domain differs from the anchor's. Exits 0 or the write is rejected.
stages.cost: 0 agents, ~10s CPU. One-time build of the tariff census and the extraction cache.

stages.stage: S3 — Seeding: canaries planted before any reviewer sees the section
stages.who: authoring agent (isolated seeder; never communicates with the prosecutors and never appears in their context)
stages.input: The section that survived S1 and S2, plus a canary recipe bank derived from the 18 confirmed criticals and the 15-class failure taxonomy (e.g. invert a real-world causal claim; mis-key an MCQ where two options are defensible; move a concept off its spec bullet; pad a levels rubric with point credits; sequence a flow so block 3 assumes block 1).
stages.passCondition: Exactly six defects injected into the review copy: one static-tier plus five judgement-tier, one owned by each prosecutor brief and one unowned. Manifest written to audit/gate/canaries/<section>.sealed.json, its sha256 minted as a ledger id via `ledger.mjs add`. Re-running S1 on the mutated copy must flag the static canary and must flag none of the five judgement canaries — if code can see a canary, that canary tests nothing and is regenerated. Objective, arithmetic, no judgement.

stages.stage: S4 — Prosecution: four conflicting briefs, no shared context, census not top-N
stages.input: R1 EXAMINER: spec extract, fingerprinted tariff table, the real mark-scheme text for the anchor's unit, section JSON. R2 FACT-CHECKER: section JSON only, no spec, no other reviewer — must quote the sentence and state the correct fact. R3 EXPLOITER: only what a student sees, with the teaching prose withheld; must answer every quiz, recall and fill-in blind and report its score. R4 PEDAGOGUE: section JSON plus research-pedagogy-critique.md; owns sequencing, difficulty ramp, redundancy, whether a flow is a causal chain or three facts with arrows. None sees another's output; none sees the canary manifest; none is ever asked for 'the top N issues'.
stages.passCondition: Four arithmetic checks a session runs without judgement. (1) For each brief, reviewedItemCount equals the artefact counts in audit/raw/section-index.json for the classes it owns — a reviewer that skips items fails by subtraction. (2) quote-check.mjs re-finds every cited quote byte-for-byte in the section JSON; zero unresolvable quotes. (3) R3 returns a numeric blind score and it is within 10 points of chance (25% on 4-option MCQ) — today the corpus scores 64% by always answering B. (4) No brief returned a bounded list. A brief failing any check is re-run with a fresh agent, never patched.
stages.cost: 4 agents, ~100k input tokens each; ~15 minutes wall in parallel

stages.stage: S5 — Defence: one skeptic per surviving finding, refute mandate
stages.input: The finding, the section, the spec extract — and deliberately NOT the prosecutor's reasoning, not the builder's conversation, not the other findings. Told the finding is probably wrong. This is the prompt shape that produced 88 verdicts on the code findings, 6 refutations and 10+ severity corrections.
stages.passCondition: Every finding has a verdict record carrying refuted true/false, correctedSeverity, and verbatim evidence that re-finds in the file. Every non-refuted finding is minted as a ledger id. The severity written to the ledger is the skeptic's, never the finder's — measured behaviour is that finders inflate (25 of 88 verdicts contain 'inflat*', no finding retained critical after verification).
stages.cost: 10–25 agents at ~10k tokens each; parallel, ~10 minutes wall

stages.stage: S6 — Scoring the reviewers, not the section
stages.who: static check (arithmetic over the sealed manifest)
stages.input: The sealed canary manifest from S3, unsealed for the first time, and the union of prosecution findings from S4/S5. Union, never intersection: two agents on an identical brief overlapped at Jaccard 0.087, so demanding consensus would discard most of what a panel finds.
stages.passCondition: All six canaries appear in the union AND each brief-owned canary was caught by its owning brief (an accidental catch by the wrong brief does not count). A brief that misses its own canary is VOID: its entire output is discarded and it re-runs once with a fresh agent and a fresh canary. Two consecutive misses retires that brief, blocks the section and escalates to the founder. Per-brief recall is appended to audit/gate/scoreboard.csv so a degrading brief is visible across 43 sections. This is the only mechanism in the design that attacks reviewer blind spots rather than assuming they cancel out.

stages.stage: S7 — Ablation exam: does reading this section move a mark?
stages.who: review agent ×3 (two proxy students, one grader)
stages.input: Three real past-paper questions for the unit whose spec points this section owns, taken structurally from past_papers. Student A reads only this section. Student B reads only a decoy section from the other subject. The grader reads neither section — only the real mark scheme's level grid and the two anonymised scripts.
stages.passCondition: Two numbers, both committed. (1) Grader's mark for A minus B is at least +30% of the marks available on this section's own spec points; a section that does not move the mark is not teaching, whatever it looks like. (2) The grader enumerates every named-entity, date and figure claim in A's script; zero of them may be traceable to a section sentence and contradicted by the mark scheme or by the grader's own check. Any such trace is an automatic critical and reopens the section. This is the only stage that catches a factual error at the point where it does harm — a student repeating the inverted Toyota JIT story in an answer — rather than by fact-checking prose.

stages.stage: S8 — Founder spot-check: symptoms only, three questions
stages.input: Exactly four artefacts, selected by script and not by the builder: the highest-tariff practice item; one realExample drawn at random; the single highest corrected-severity open finding; and Student A's 20-mark script with the mark the grader gave it. No mechanism, no diff, no reviewer reasoning, no answer key. This split is evidence-based: the founder's own report was ~1/3 grounded on mechanism (6 of 10 claims FALSE) but reliable on symptom.
stages.passCondition: Three recorded answers plus one free-text box: (a) does this look like a question from the paper? (b) is this claim true — would you say it to a student? (c) does that mark look right for that script? Any 'no' reopens the section and is converted into a ledger id verbatim; it is never argued with or re-explained. Recorded in NEXT.md under the packet spec, so a verifier can check the answers exist without re-litigating them.

stages.stage: S9 — Close and ratchet
stages.who: static check + the existing packet-verifier agent (read-only, fresh context)
stages.input: The packet diff, audit/ledger.json, all 43 section snapshots.
stages.passCondition: All of: `node audit/scripts/ledger.mjs unverified <n>` exits 0; `npm run gate -- --all` exits 0 on BLOCK across all 43 sections (a regression detector, explicitly demoted from being the gate — PLAN.md line 94 already warns that a gate beside the write path is a convention, and March had one of those); `npm run build` green; the canary scoreboard row written; a provenance lint showing zero createClient( calls under scripts/, seed/ or audit/scripts/ outside _db.mjs; and the section goes live through packet 2's draft→published switch as one statement, not row by row.

catches: Every structural class that is 54.9% of the measured failures — exam shape, untaught assessment, MCQ construction, wiring, recall design — at S1/S2 before any agent is spent on it. Measured against the live corpus these rules fire on 198 of 215 practice items, 322 of 769 quiz items, 141 of 141 fill-in hint leaks, 99 of 131 reused reorder permutations, 648 orphaned quiz items and 3 dangling diagram refs.

The answer-position exploit, and it catches it as a number rather than an assertion. R3's blind score is the pass condition, so the corpus-wide defect that no section reviewer could see (492 of 769 keys on index B; always answering B scores 64% platform-wide) fails the gate automatically on any future section.

Tariff, command word, AO split, level grid, band boundaries and ceiling rules anchored to the 72 real mark schemes rather than to the spec appendix — which matters because WBS11 Oct-2022 Q1(e) is an 'Analyse' worth 10 marks on the Assess-10 grid, a shape the appendix does not predict.

Copyright, on both fronts the founder actually faces: n-gram overlap against all 86 extracted PDFs plus a forced scenario-domain change blocks the 'same stem, new company name' paraphrase, and every item carries a provenance record naming the paper it imitates — facts and formats, never expression.

The contaminated reference data, by fingerprinting it. The gate refuses to run against an unsigned audit/ref/, so nothing can silently inherit the nine non-IAL command words that almost certainly drove the March generation.

Rubber-stamping, through four independent mechanisms with evidence behind each: census arithmetic instead of top-N (enumerated classes hit 100% coverage in September; sampled prose hit a 6–15 quota regardless of section size), verbatim quote re-verification (already caught 2 of 88 mis-citations), reviewer isolation, and severity set by an adversary who never saw the finder's reasoning.

A measured error rate for the reviewers themselves. The canary scoreboard is the one thing March's validator and the September audit both lack entirely — after five sections there is a per-brief recall number, and a brief that degrades is retired on evidence rather than on vibes.

A meaningful share of the judgement tier. Four conflicting briefs plus a refutation pass should at least match one reviewer per section, which found all 18 confirmed criticals; R4 owns the 161 sequencing failures nobody else was briefed on; and S7 catches the subset of factual errors a student would actually repeat in a marked answer.

Process rot in the two places it actually happened: the write-path proxy converts 93 scripts without their cooperation, and the provenance lint blocks the next file that builds its own client — the hole that let 17 files, including a September-era audit script, bypass the shared one.
misses: The deepest limit: canaries can only measure recall on failure modes we already named, and the canary bank is written by the same model family as the prosecutors. A blind spot shared between seeder and reviewer is invisible by construction — the scoreboard will read 100% while the section carries a defect no one in the loop has a concept for. Capture-recapture on the nine-lens code panel put observed defects at 85 against ~221 estimated; four briefs will do worse than nine, and the canary number will not tell you so.

Factual error in real-world examples — 184 failures, the class with the worst student-facing consequence — is only probabilistically caught. R2 and the S7 grader are models checking facts with no fact database and no guaranteed external source. An inverted claim that the reviewing model also believes (the Toyota JIT story reads plausibly) passes every stage. Nothing in this design is a source of truth about the world.

The gate measures the artefact; the founder's bar is about the student. The S7 delta is a proxy-student delta, and a language model carrying latent A-level economics is not a 16-year-old in Karachi who has never seen the material. A positive delta says the section is not inert; it does not say a student is prepared. The only instrument that could answer the founder's actual question is real student marks on the 75 real papers already sitting in his database, and that instrument does not exist yet in any packet.

Every mechanical rule is a target the authoring agent optimises against, and the author is the same kind of model as the reviewers. The stricter the checkable surface gets, the more the failure migrates to the uncheckable one — this is not speculation, it is exactly what happened on meeting-customer-needs, where guidance credits were padded to sum to the tariff. Adversarial review moves that boundary; it does not remove it.

The pass condition 'zero open critical or high' rests on severity, which is precisely where AI review is measurably worst: all 6 of 88 refutations were severity overturns and no finding retained 'critical' after verification. The gate's strictness is therefore set by the judgement its own panel is least reliable at making.

Every reliability figure quoted here is transferred from code review. All 88 adversarial verdicts cite .jsx/.js/.css/.sql; zero cite content. No content finding in this repo has ever been second-opinioned, so the 6.8% disagreement rate may simply be wrong for prose about economics.

A per-section gate is structurally blind to the corpus. The answer-B skew, the six reused shuffle permutations, the 372-term glossary, the 18-row command-word table and cross-section duplication were invisible to 43 section reviewers and would be invisible to this gate too. S9's full-corpus sweep and packets 13/57 are the only cover, and they are sweeps, not gates.

Only two parts of this design cannot be skipped: the write-path proxy and the `unverified` exit code. The prosecution stages, the canaries and the ablation exam are enforced by the packet gate and by the founder's willingness to reject a packet at 11pm — which is a convention, the exact failure mode that made March's validator optional in 22 of 43 scripts. Expect the first skipped stage within ten sections and instrument for it.

It is free in money and not free in tokens: roughly 20–30 agent runs and 0.4–1.0M subagent tokens per section, so ~30M across 43 sections. Under PROTOCOL's 'a few million subagent tokens' rule that is a budget the founder must approve up front, not discover.

12 founder minutes is the steady state, not the start. Budget ~45 minutes each for the first five sections while canary recall is being calibrated and briefs are being tuned, and treat any section where he answers 'no' twice as a signal that a brief is broken, not that the section is unlucky.

Two things this gate does not touch at all: the live world-readable Supabase bucket redistributing 86 Pearson-copyright PDFs (fix that today, independently of any of this), and the fact that detection is not repair — every stage produces a blocking signal and a work queue, and the authoring itself stays in the judgement tier no matter how good the checks get.
designs.firstThingToBuild: audit/scripts/gate/ — the four prosecutor brief files plus calibrate.mjs — run against three already-audited t=0 sections and scored against the 2,088 existing labels in audit/raw/content-audits.json, producing one number per brief: what fraction of what a reviewer already found does this brief recover, and what does it find that the September reviewer missed. It needs no authoring, no DB write, no reference data and no founder time, and it is the only way to learn the panel's error rate before 42 sections depend on it. Build it before packet 14 authors a single item; if recall against known labels is poor, the design is wrong and you find out for free. Packet 3's static gate (S1/S2) proceeds in parallel as already scoped — it is necessary, but it is not the risky part of this design, and it is the part that does not need proving.

designs.name: Anchor and Sit
designs.premise: A mark scheme is a free examiner that never gets tired: 635 real question stems and their grids, extracted once from the 86 PDFs already in the founder's own bucket, tell you exactly what Edexcel asks and rewards — so every authored item is gated on measured agreement with that corpus, and the gate's own claim is then falsified or survived by having one agent sit the real questions having read only our section and another sit them blind, with the difference between them as the pass condition.

stages.stage: S0. Shape Bank + Topic Anchor Index (built once, before packet 14, never per section)
stages.input: The 86 PDFs read with the service key from the past-papers bucket AFTER it is made private; audit/raw/econ_spec.txt and bus_spec.txt; audit/raw/research-ial-spec-coverage.md. Extraction happens in a gitignored workspace. The committed artefact stores FACTS ONLY — per (subject, unit, command, marks): marking_mode, ao_split shapes with sighting counts, level-grid count and exact band boundaries, ceiling rules, QS codes, and a citation of paper code + session + question number. Stem text is read to derive topic tags and then discarded; it is never committed.
stages.passCondition: `node audit/scripts/build-shape-bank.mjs --verify` exits 0, which asserts: (a) every shape row carries >=2 sightings each with paper code, session and question number; (b) all 72 mark-scheme files yield >=1 parsed stem, so there are no silent zero-yield files (my seed parser already gets 635 stems from 72/72 — the earlier attempt got 284 from 58); (c) the committed JSON shares no 8-gram with any extracted PDF text; (d) each of the 43 sections has a topic-coverage flag in {DIRECT, ADJACENT, NONE}; (e) command_words.json is regenerated from the corpus, which empirically contains zero occurrences of Outline, Identify, Describe, Suggest, Justify, Distinguish and Consider across all 635 stems.
stages.cost: 1 agent, roughly one session, once for all 43 sections

stages.stage: S1. Static gate inside the write path (not beside it)
stages.input: The payload being written, plus the Shape Bank, the spec-bullet keyword map, the off-spec denylist and the n-gram index of the 86 texts. Implemented as an isomorphic lib/validate/index.mjs called from (i) a wrapped client in scripts/_db.mjs whose .from() proxies the eight content tables and validates inside then(), (ii) app/api/admin/sections/[id]/[type]/route.js returning 422, (iii) a thin Postgres BEFORE trigger holding only the three invariants that must never be bypassed.
stages.passCondition: 0 BLOCK findings. Every DEBT finding carries a ledger id and an owning packet. The success report prints the number of rules that ran and an explicit list of what it did NOT check, and never prints the word 'passed'. `node audit/scripts/validator-sweep.mjs` green on all 43 sections. `grep -rn 'createClient(' scripts/ seed/ audit/scripts/ | grep -v _db.mjs` returns nothing, so the 17 files that currently build their own client cannot reopen the March hole.

stages.stage: S2. Blind exploit run — can the assessment be beaten without the teaching?
stages.input: The section's quiz, recall and fill-in items with all teaching prose, explanations and answer keys stripped out. The agent must answer and then list the surface cues it used.
stages.passCondition: MCQ score <= 35% (four-option chance plus 10 points); per-section correctIndex chi-square p > 0.05; zero fill-ins answered correctly from the hint alone; the agent's reported cue list is empty. Today the live corpus fails this outright: always answering B scores 64.0% platform-wide (492 of 769), the keyed option is the longest in 474 of 769, and 141 of 141 fill-in hints prefix their answer.

stages.stage: S3. Three-brief census on a canaried copy
stages.input: A temp copy of the section with 3 defects seeded from the held-out bank of 18 confirmed criticals (one wrong tariff, one false named-entity fact, one mis-keyed MCQ). R1 EXAMINER gets the Shape Bank plus one real mark scheme for that unit. R2 FACT-CHECKER gets the section JSON only — no spec, no other reviewer. R3 SPEC-MAPPER gets the spec bullet text. Briefs are distinct, not redundant: two agents on an identical brief overlapped at Jaccard 0.087.
stages.passCondition: Each reviewer's enumerated item count equals the inventory in audit/raw/section-index.json, so a reviewer that samples fails arithmetically. All 3 canaries found by the brief that owns each class. `audit/scripts/quote-check.mjs` re-finds 100% of finding quotes verbatim in the file. The canary marker strings appear 0 times in the payload actually published. Never ask any reviewer for 'the top N issues' — the quota artefact is visible in the September data (accuracy findings cluster at 6-15 per section regardless of section size, while enumerated classes hit 100%).

stages.stage: S4. Adversary pass, one agent per surviving finding
stages.input: One finding, the section and the spec — never the reviewer's reasoning, never the builder's conversation. Mandate is to refute.
stages.passCondition: Every finding returns refuted true/false plus correctedSeverity plus verbatim evidence. Zero findings left open at corrected severity critical or high. Expect it to recalibrate rather than discover: on the 88 code verdicts it refuted 6, all of them severity overturns, and killed 0 findings on fact.

stages.stage: S5. The sit — paired, blinded, three runs
stages.input: Real past-paper questions for that spec bullet where coverage is DIRECT, or the adjacent bullet where it is ADJACENT/NONE. TAUGHT agents get only the student-facing section. BLIND agents get only the questions. A separate GRADER agent gets the real mark-scheme grid and the two scripts anonymised, in random order, and must not be told which condition is which.
stages.passCondition: Taught >= 60% of marks available; taught minus blind >= +15 percentage points on the levels-marked questions; zero questions where blind outscores taught; the grader cites the band and quotes the exact credited sentence for every award; the delta is positive in all 3 paired runs. Absolute marks from a model grader are not trustworthy, so the pass condition is the within-question paired delta under blinded condition labels, which survives a miscalibrated grader.

stages.stage: S6. Founder sample — symptoms only, never mechanism
stages.input: One page: one authored practice item printed beside its Shape Bank row and one real stem from the same unit; the single highest corrected-severity surviving finding; two realExamples flagged as named-entity-plus-year-plus-figure; the sit's taught-vs-blind delta with one quoted credited sentence.
stages.passCondition: Five prompts, each answered looks-right / looks-wrong / don't-know. Any looks-wrong or don't-know on a factual claim DELETES that claim — it never opens a research task, because his own report fact-check scored roughly a third grounded and he is reliable on symptom, not on mechanism. Answers recorded in NEXT.md under the packet spec.

stages.stage: S7. Packet close, unchanged from the existing protocol
stages.input: audit/ledger.json, the build, the validator sweep, the canary log
stages.passCondition: `npm run build` green; `node audit/scripts/ledger.mjs unverified <n>` exits 0; validator sweep green on all 43; a per-brief canary-recall row appended to audit/canary-log.json so a degrading brief can be retired on evidence; PROGRESS.md row updated; commit prefixed `packet-<n>:`.

catches: Every exam-shape defect, which is the largest single class. The (subject, unit, command, marks) tuple check against a corpus-derived Shape Bank kills 173 of the 215 live practice items on a table lookup, and the September reviewers independently flagged 171 of those 173, so this class is now mechanised at 98.8% agreement with a human-grade reviewer for zero marginal cost.

Command words that do not exist in IAL. Outline, Identify, Describe, Suggest, Justify, Distinguish and Consider appear exactly 0 times across all 635 real stems I parsed, yet 9 of the 18 rows in the app's own command_words.json are drawn from that set and 'Examine' and 'Construct' are missing. S0 regenerates that table from the corpus, so the reference data stops being part of the failure.

The two structurally different marking machineries. Economics levels questions split across two grids (KAA plus a separate Evaluation grid); Business uses one combined KAAE ladder, and only Business Evaluate 20 requires a recommendation. Band boundaries were identical in every sighting, so exact-match on boundaries is a hard check an AI author will otherwise get wrong by default.

Unmarkable levels items. Every levels question in the real corpus is anchored to an extract, figure or named business; 62 live items use a levels tariff with no stimulus at all, and 0 of 215 both match a real tariff and carry a stimulus. Requiring a non-empty authored stimulus for marking_mode=levels is checkable and unarguable.

Assessment that can be beaten without learning. The B-skew (492 of 769 keyed to index 1, 64% platform-wide), longest-option cue (474 of 769), hint-prefix leakage (141 of 141 fill-ins), and reorder permutation reuse (99 of 131 on two permutations). S1 blocks them and S2 measures whether any cue survived.

Content that is not taught or not on the spec. Term-presence against the section's own taught text triages the 296-failure untaught-assessment class; the spec-bullet keyword map covers the 169 spec-gap class; the off-spec denylist catches 469 live hits of deadweight, merit/demerit good, accelerator, nudge and bounded rationality that appear 0 times in the official spec text.

Wiring, localisation and unsourced authority. 648 orphan quiz items, 151 orphan practice items, 22 sections with identity-sequence quizIndices, 3 dangling diagramRefs, 130 UK-only token occurrences across 26 sections, and 244 'Examiners reward/penalise' sentences with zero citations — all pure static, all invisible to the March validator.

Verbatim copyright exposure. An 8-gram overlap check against the extracted text of all 86 PDFs blocks any authored stem, stimulus or rubric that reproduces Pearson expression, and the Shape Bank itself is facts-only (command, tariff, AO split, band boundaries, ceilings, QS codes, citations) with stem text discarded at build time, so the repo never carries the protected material.

The bypass that actually caused March. The gate lives in the write path — a proxied client in _db.mjs that converts 93 scripts by editing one file, the admin PUT route returning 422, and a three-invariant Postgres trigger — plus a lint that blocks any new createClient() outside _db.mjs. In March the check was a function you had to remember to paste, and the 22 scripts that did not paste it are exactly the 22 sections that fail it today.

Lazy or degrading review. Census counts must equal inventory, every quote must re-find verbatim in the file, severity is set by an adversary that never sees the finder's reasoning, and 3 seeded canaries per section void any brief that misses one — with per-brief recall logged over time so a brief can be retired on evidence rather than vibes.
misses: Factual truth of real-world examples, which is the class with the worst student-facing consequence. 184 failures (9.1%) of the Toyota-JIT-inverted, Tesla-financing-invented, eBay-sold-Skype-to-Microsoft kind. My only defence is the R2 fact-checker agent, and content review in this repo has NEVER been adversarially verified: all 88 verdicts cite code files, 0 cite content. The model class that wrote the invented Tesla financing in March is the model class I am asking to catch it, and its error rate is unmeasured. The canary bank is 18 items of which roughly 6 are factual — enough to detect gross blindness, nowhere near enough to estimate recall. If you asked me for the probability that a false named-entity claim ships in packet 14, I could not give you a number, and nothing in this design produces one.

Conceptual errors in the taught prose (106 failures) — transfer payments as an injection, loan repayments as a fixed cost, a plc defined by stock-exchange listing. Mark schemes reward answers; they do not teach, so calibration against papers gives no oracle here at all. This is the part of the design where the bet on real papers simply does not pay.

Whether a reasoning chain is genuinely multi-stage cause-and-consequence or assertion with connectives — precisely the Economics KAA Level 2/3 boundary. The S5 grader claims to judge it and nothing verifies the grader. The blinded paired delta protects the comparison, not the absolute standard.

The sit measures whether the section CONTAINS and organises what the mark scheme rewards. It does not measure whether a 17-year-old on a phone at 390px can learn it from there. Difficulty ramp, sequencing and cognitive load (161 failures) are untouched, and an LLM ingesting 4,000 words in one pass is not a student. A section could pass every stage and still be unlearnable.

The taught-vs-blind delta is noisy and partly gameable by its own subjects. The blind agent already knows economics, so the delta understates real teaching value; the taught agent may credit knowledge it already had, so the delta overstates it. Three paired runs bound the variance, they do not remove the confound, and the +15pp threshold is a number I invented and can only calibrate on packet 14.

Topic calibration does not exist for every section. Measuring strictly, 5 of 43 sections have ZERO question stems in five years of their unit's papers that mention their own title vocabulary (assessing-competitiveness, financial-planning, managing-people, meeting-customer-needs, introductory-concepts) and 10 of 43 have fewer than three. For those the design degrades to shape-only anchoring plus adjacent-bullet sits, which means the central bet is not actually being made there — and meeting-customer-needs is the second-highest-traffic section on the platform.

The corpus stops at October 2024 and only 11 of 75 slots have both paper and mark scheme. MCQ shape and stimulus length are calibrated from 14 question papers; any 2025-26 drift in emphasis or format is invisible, and 61 anchors give marking shape without the question that shape was built for.

Every mechanical rule is a target for the agent authoring the content. It can hit the tariff, the AO split, the band boundaries, the credit-token counts and the stimulus word floor and still write a question no examiner would set — padded credits are literally the defect the audit already found on meeting-customer-needs. The stricter the checkable surface becomes, the more the failure migrates into the uncheckable one, and the gate is blind to that migration by construction.

Calibrating the gate against audit/raw/content-audits.json measures agreement with one unverified reviewer, not with an examiner. Recall of 98.8% on the tariff class is recall against that reviewer. Whole artefact classes were barely reviewed at all (844 flashcards drew 7 findings, 306 extras drew 1), so the golden set is silent exactly where I most need a baseline.

Twelve founder minutes samples roughly four of about sixty items per section. If one item in ten is still defective after every stage, he sees a defective one about a third of the time. His sample detects systemic rot across packets; it does not catch individual bad items, and it must never be described to him as if it did.

The terminal question — is a student who revised here as prepared as one who used expert material — is not decidable by any of this. It is decided by real students' marks on real papers, which needs a cohort and a term and does not exist today. This design makes the content defensible. Only student marks would make it verified, and the honest status of every section that passes is 'no known defects of 40 checkable kinds, plus three agent opinions and twelve minutes of a non-examiner's attention'.
designs.firstThingToBuild: `audit/scripts/build-shape-bank.mjs` — the one-time, facts-only extraction that produces audit/fixtures/shape-bank.json and topic-anchors.json from the 86 PDFs, plus a regenerated command_words.json and the 8-gram index used by the copyright check. Build it first because every later stage reads it, because it is the artefact that makes the copyright line enforceable (stems read in a gitignored workspace and discarded; only command, tariff, AO split, grid boundaries, ceilings, QS codes and paper/question citations are committed), and because it converts the founder's largest live exposure into a prerequisite: the script reads with the service key, which is only correct once the world-readable past-papers bucket is made private — do that in the same session, before anything else, since 86 Pearson-copyright PDFs are currently served to anyone with the URL and no gate offsets a distribution act. Seed it with the parser I already validated here: 635 stems from 72 of 72 mark schemes, zero occurrences of Outline / Identify / Describe / Suggest / Justify / Distinguish / Consider, which is the whitelist that kills 173 of the 215 live practice items on day one.

fatalFlaws: S5's canaries are unrepresentable under S1/S2 — the liveness check dies of the design's own strictness. Two of the three seeded defects are 'one invalid tariff (R1's class)' and 'one mis-keyed MCQ with two defensible options (R1/R3)'. S1 makes both unauthorable by construction: command/marks derive from a shape_id FK and correctIndex 'no longer exists'. So either the canary injector writes outside scripts/_db.mjs — directly contradicting S2's pass condition 'zero createClient( occurrences under scripts/, seed/ or audit/scripts/ outside _db.mjs' and its claim to be unbypassable — or R1's and R3's canaries cannot be injected at all and their liveness checks are vacuous. Only R2's false-fact canary survives, which is the one the author himself flags as proposed on reasoning rather than evidence. The retirement rule in DECISIONS.md then fires on one brief and never on the other two.

R2 — the sole defence against the admitted-worst class — is the one brief that cannot be census-counted. S4's anti-rubber-stamp condition is 'reviewed_item_count == the section's count in audit/raw/section-index.json for the artefact classes that brief owns'. R2 owns realExamples and named-entity claims. `grep -c realExample audit/raw/section-index.json` returns 0: the index carries blocks, subsections, reorder, fillin, quiz, practice, diagrams, flashcards, notes, mistakes, extrasChains, extrasEval — nothing R2 owns. Meanwhile 413 realExample fields exist in audit/content-sections/ (mean 9.6/section, max 24) and 182 of the 453 accuracy issues (40.2%) are located in realExample. So the mechanism the design is proudest of, the one that 'turned recall review into a 272/272 census', is arithmetically inapplicable to the brief carrying 290 failures, and R2 must instead free-read a median 9,625-word section (max 15,854) with no coverage obligation.

S6 gives the veto to the worse-informed party and pre-loads it toward acquittal. R2's inputs include 'web search allowed'; S6's inputs are 'the finding, the section, the spec' — no search. An adversary with strictly less evidence than the finder, explicitly 'told the finding is probably wrong and given a refute mandate', is the only authority over severity, and the pass condition is 'zero findings remain open at corrected severity critical or high'. A downgrade therefore closes a finding. The design's own cited behaviour — 6 of 88 code verdicts, 6.8%, 'all of them severity overturns' — is precisely the behaviour that empties the blocking set. At ~20 findings across 43 sections that is roughly 58 findings removed from blocking by a blind agent with an acquittal prior. This is a rubber stamp with arithmetic painted on it.

Nothing in the design checks spec coverage, and S3 pushes against it. 340 ialSpecGaps — the second-largest class in the audit, 16.9% of 2,013 — are absence defects (e.g. globalisation: '4.1.4 Protectionism: tariffs, import quotas, other trade barriers ... entirely absent from content[]'; price-determination: '1.3.4 3(b) The price mechanism in the context of different types of markets ... not taught anywhere (no subsection, no example, no recall, no MCQ)'). S2 checks that 'spec_bullet resolves' — per-item presence, not per-section coverage. S0 emits fixtures/spec-bullets.json but no pass condition consumes it for coverage. Worse, S3's requirement that assessment be unbeatable without the prose is trivially satisfied by narrowing what the section covers; there is no counter-pressure toward breadth anywhere in the gate.

S3's threshold is arithmetically unachievable and will be the first number relaxed. The bar is 'MCQ score <= 35% (4-option chance 25% + 10pp)', justified by heuristic baselines. I reproduced those baselines exactly against audit/content-sections/: 769 MCQs, 492 keyed to index 1 (64.0%), 540 where the key is the longest option (70.2%), 39 of 43 sections >=50% on one index. But S3 is a Sonnet agent, not a heuristic — nothing in its brief restricts it to surface features, and a frontier model answering IAL Economics MCQs blind scores far above 35% from pretraining alone, on correctly authored items. S3 as specified fails every section forever, including expert-authored ones. It is the design's only student-facing number, and it is the exact shape of `pin-check --max-broken 15` that the author names in his own admissions: a threshold with no owner that gets retuned at section 20.

The dominant MCQ exploit is neither position nor blocked. The design credits the balanced allocator with killing 'MCQ construction skew (201)'; the allocator kills position only. The exploit the reviewers actually name is test-wiseness via absolutes — meeting-customer-needs: 'three distractors use absolutes (eliminates all risk, guarantees, only), making the answer trivially the hedged option. Tests test-wiseness, not content'; the-market: 'the only hedged option ... is correct, the other three are absolutes ... students learn pick the longest option'; global-marketing Q7: 'Distractors Asian consumers do not watch television and Competitors in Asia do not have brand names are absurd rather than plausible; the item cannot discriminate'. 48 quizIssues name hedging/plausibility directly; 157 of 398 touch guessability. The design assigns 'longest-correct-option' to the DEBT tier — 'never a build failure'.

The largest single quiz defect class is on the non-blocking worklist. 103 of 398 quizIssues name untaught / off-spec / wrong-unit material (global-marketing: 'Quiz/content mismatch: 5 of 10 MCQs (indices 1,3,4,6,8) examine terms never taught in content[] ... The PreTest draws 3 random items from this bank, so roughly half of pretests will contain untaught material'). The design's rule for this is 'glossary-term-not-taught', explicitly DEBT: 'emit a worklist handed to S4, never a build failure'. The biggest class gets the weakest tier.

S3 pays authors to produce the worst recall class. recallAudit verdicts across 272 items: genuine-sequence 64, fine 11, hint-leaks-answer 51, trivial 66, weak-or-arbitrary-sequence 48, not-orderable 18, ambiguous-answers 14. Deleting the hint field kills 51; deleting the stored `shuffled` array kills permutation reuse but says nothing about whether a sequence exists. 146 items (trivial + weak + not-orderable + ambiguous) are owned by no brief — R3 is scoped to 'cross-surface contradiction and term-first-use ordering'. And S3 actively rewards the worst of them: an arbitrary reorder such as the PPF item 'On the curve -> Inside -> Outside -> Slope' is unsolvable blind precisely because any order is defensible, so it scores perfectly against '<= 1 recall widget solved without the prose'.

S0's shipping gate is circular. Condition (d) requires the replay to flag 'exactly 173 of 215 practice items and 123 of 215 on the (command, marks) rule alone', and says a different number means 'the fixture must not ship'. Both numbers are outputs of the same parser and fixture being validated; the cheap resolution under packet pressure is to tune the fixture until it prints 173. I censused the live corpus (Economics: Define-4 23, Explain-6 23, Evaluate-20 23, Outline-4 23, Assess-10 20, Analyse-10 3; Business: Explain-4 20, Evaluate-20 20, Assess-10 19, Explain-6 13, Analyse-6 10, Define-4 10, Outline-4 7, Analyse-10 1) and could not reach 123 under any single consistent invalidity rule — plausible sets land at 109 or 132. Conditions (a) and (b) (n_sightings >= 2, resolving paper citation) are the real validation; (d) is self-reference dressed as rigour.

The n-gram BLOCK rule and S7's question are in direct conflict, and the block wins. Median practice stem is 15 words; 72 of 215 are <=12 words. Correct IAL phrasing is the paper's phrasing — audit/content-sections/economics__supply.json practice[0] reads "Define the term 'price elasticity of supply' (PES)." A BLOCK-tier n-gram check with no override against 86 Pearson PDFs either passes everything (loose threshold, so the copyright claim is empty) or drives authors to un-IAL phrasing to clear it — manufacturing a new defect in exactly the place S7 is meant to detect it ('would this look at home on a WEC11 paper').
wouldLetThrough: types-sizes-businesses, critical: "'eBay demerged Skype in 2009, selling it to Microsoft' is wrong on two counts ... eBay sold a ~65-70% stake to an investor group led by Silver Lake; Microsoft bought Skype in 2011 ... selling a subsidiary to a third party is a divestment/sell-off, not a demerger." Every structural rule passes. Only R2 can catch it; S6 (no web search, refute mandate) can downgrade it; S7 shows the founder 'the three realExamples R2 marked verified-true', i.e. R2's pass pile, so if R2 misses it the founder never sees it.

the-market, critical, realExample: "UK strawberry retail prices are LOWEST in summer because that is peak season ... Presented as 'the law of supply in action' (movement along the curve), it is a textbook example of the opposite." Correctly tariffed, correctly located, no UK-token trigger beyond 'UK' (which the uk-tokens denylist may flag for localisation, not for teaching the law of supply backwards). The concept inversion is invisible to every static rule and to S3, which withholds the prose.

national-income, examMatters: "'these are government spending (injection) even though they are not payment for output' ... Edexcel IAL treats G in AD as spending on goods and services and excludes transfer payments; quiz[13] in this very section says transfer payments are excluded from GDP."
