The 146 recall items verdicted trivial (66), weak-or-arbitrary-sequence (48), not-orderable (18) and ambiguous-answers (14). Example: the PPF reorder 'On the curve -> Inside -> Outside -> Slope' — "Four independent facts about a diagram. There is no temporal or causal relation; any order is equally correct." No brief owns 'is this a real sequence'; S1 only removes the stored permutation; and S3's blind-solve metric scores these items best because they are unsolvable by anyone, including the student who is marked wrong for a defensible order.

Four of the eight command words in each taxonomy are absent from all 215 live practice items — Calculate 0, Draw/Construct 0, Discuss 0, Examine 0 (live census: Explain 56, Evaluate 43, Assess 39, Define 33, Outline 30, Analyse 14). research-ial-spec-coverage.md gives Economics as Define 2 / Calculate 2-4 / Draw 4 / Explain 4 / Analyse 6 / Examine 8 / Discuss 14 / Evaluate 20 and notes 'Quantitative skills are at least 20% of marks (Appendix 7) ... every paper has a Draw/Calculate item'. S2 blocks only 'no Calculate item in the set'. A section passes the entire gate with zero Discuss-14 and zero Draw items — Discuss 14 plus Evaluate 20 is 42.5% of an Economics Unit 1 paper.

The 340 ialSpecGaps as a class. 56 of them are themselves hedged ('Unsure', 'verify against the current spec PDF'), so calibrating anything against content-audits.json inherits an unverified reviewer's guesses about spec numbering — and no stage in the design checks that a section teaches the bullets it owns, only that items point at bullets that exist.
critiques.costRealism: Not honest. Eight minutes buys the founder 1 of 5 practice items (20%), 3 of a mean 9.6 realExamples (31%), 1 of ~10-25 findings, and 1 number — against a median section of 80,915 bytes JSON / ~9,625 words of prose (max 131,196 bytes / 15,854 words), 17.9 quiz items, 18 flashcards and 3.95 blocks. He reads zero words of the prose body, where 201 of 453 accuracy issues live (body 121, examMatters 56, keyIdea 24). Three problems compound this. (1) The sample is drawn from the wrong pile: S7 shows 'the three realExamples R2 marked verified-true'. realExample is the highest-defect-density field in the corpus — 182 of 453 accuracy issues against 413 realExample fields, so roughly 44% of them carried a defect in March. His minutes are spent re-checking R2's confident passes and zero minutes on the ~6.6 examples per section R2 could not verify. (2) Question 2 is either much longer than 8 minutes or worthless: 'do you believe these three claims' about eBay/Skype-shaped fabrications requires actually checking dates, entities and the concept, and the author concedes he will wave a well-formed false example through. At the stated budget the only achievable mode is a vibe check, which measures nothing. (3) No rework budget is costed. S7 states 'Any no or hold reopens the section at S2', S5 misses re-run a brief, and the base rate of a section needing rework is high (38 C, 5 D, 2,013 findings). The honest figure is 8 x (1 + reopen rate) and the design does not state the reopen rate. Orchestration is counted as zero throughout: roughly 1,060 agent runs (43 x [1 S3 + 3 S4 + ~10-25 S6], plus 9 x 3 for S8 and 2 per packet) do not start themselves, and PROTOCOL.md mandates one packet per session with a human-written ~5-minute brief and a handoff rewrite. The 45-minute figure for packet 14 is the only place the design admits the first instance costs more than the steady state; the same should be said of every section where S7 returns hold. Realistic total human cost is closer to 12-15 hours than 5.7, and that is before the S3 threshold is renegotiated.
changes: Fix the canary contradiction or delete the claim. Seed canaries by mutating the serialized section JSON handed to each reviewer copy, after schema validation, never in the database — so no write path bypasses S2 and R1/R3 canaries become representable again. Publish the mutation script and its manifest. If that is not done, remove the R1 and R3 canaries from S5 and stop describing the panel as liveness-checked.

Give R2 a census it can be counted against. Add realExamples, examMattersClaims and namedEntities counts to audit/raw/section-index.json (today: zero occurrences of 'realExample'), and require every realExample to carry a structured claim record — entity, date, figure, source URL, verified true/false/unverifiable. Then S4's 'reviewed_item_count == the section's count' applies to the brief that carries 290 failures instead of skipping it.

Invert S7. Show the founder the realExamples R2 could NOT verify plus one it could, unlabelled, and show the highest-severity finding S6 downgraded rather than the highest one left open. Same eight minutes, aimed at the residual instead of at the consensus. Add a fifth item: one spec bullet the section claims to teach, with the founder asked 'is this actually taught here'.

Give S6 web search, or strip its authority over factual findings. An adversary with less evidence than the finder must not be able to close what the finder opened. Change the pass condition from 'zero findings remain open at corrected severity critical or high' to 'zero open at critical or high AND every downgrade carries a verbatim cited source' — a downgrade with no source is not a verdict, and the 6.8%/all-severity-overturns precedent says that is exactly what will arrive.

Replace S3's agent with three deterministic scripted exploiters — always-index-k, always-longest-option, only-non-absolute-option — run in milliseconds with zero model calls, reporting the three exploit rates separately against the measured baselines (64.0% index-1, 70.2% longest, 39/43 sections >=50% skew). Keep an LLM blind-solve as an INFO number only. As written, S3's <=35% bar measures the model's economics knowledge, fails every section including expert-authored ones, and is guaranteed to be retuned.

Promote three DEBT rules to BLOCK: longest-correct-option share above 40% per section; single-non-absolute-option / absolutes-in-distractors; and quiz-term-not-taught-in-this-section. These cover the 48 hedging findings and the 103 untaught/off-spec findings — together the largest quiz classes in the audit, currently both non-blocking.

Add a coverage gate. Every spec bullet owned by the section must have at least one content subsection AND at least one assessment item mapped to it, checked against fixtures/spec-bullets.json, with a per-section coverage percentage printed and a floor enforced. 340 ialSpecGaps are absence defects and no stage in this design can see absence.

Extend the required-shape BLOCK beyond Calculate. Per section: at least one Calculate, at least one Draw (Economics) / Construct (Business), at least one Examine-8 (Economics) / Discuss-8 (Business), at least one Discuss-14 (Economics), and at least 20% of the section's practice marks quantitative (spec Appendix 7). Live census is Calculate 0, Draw/Construct 0, Discuss 0, Examine 0 across 215 items.

Give recall items an owner. Add a fourth brief, or extend R3 explicitly: 'is this reorder a genuine causal or temporal sequence derived from a body flow of >=3 steps or an extras.chains entry, and is any other order defensible?' 146 of 272 recall items are trivial, weak, not-orderable or ambiguous, no brief owns that question, and S3 currently rewards the worst of them.

Demote S0 condition (d) from an equality gate to a reported metric. Keep (a), (b) and (c) — n_sightings >= 2 and a resolving paper citation are real external validation; 'flags exactly 173 of 215' validates the fixture against its own parser and invites tuning until the number matches.

Downgrade the n-gram rule to DEBT for stems under 25 words (72 of 215 are <=12 words; median 15) and BLOCK only on stimulus and extract prose, where the check is statistically meaningful. Otherwise the copyright rule and 'would this look at home on a WEC11 paper' pull in opposite directions and the BLOCK wins.

Replicate S8 or demote it. Three paired runs on different paper slots per checkpoint, gated on the sign of the mean delta with a stated tolerance, and the marker blinded to paper identity across repeats. 'Non-decreasing' on a single unreplicated treatment-minus-control measurement across 11 reused slots will block ships at random and will be relaxed.

Put an expiry on the DEBT tier now, in S9, not a promise. Hard cap: zero DEBT items older than two packets, and relaxing the cap requires a named DECISIONS.md entry with the packet number that pays it back. The author correctly predicts this is the first rule to go at section 20; make going there visible.

Validate the canary premise on the first five sections as the author proposes, and write the abort condition down in advance: if per-brief canary recall on organic-looking injections is below some stated figure, the brief is retired and the class it owned goes back to the founder or to a paid spot-check. Without a pre-committed number this becomes a metric that is read and never acted on.

fatalFlaws: NO STAGE CAN LOOK ANYTHING UP. 182 of 453 accuracy issues sit in `realExample` (I classified them; the design says 184) and the corpus has 413 realExamples whose schema is literally `{text, emoji}` -- I checked economics__supply.json, there is no source, date or citation field. R2 gets 'section JSON only'; the S7 grader gets 'the grader's own check'. Both are model weights. The September audit's own verdict on managing-people reads: 'Marks & Spencer restructured its hierarchy in 2022, reducing management layers from seven to five -- could not be corroborated; M&S's 2022-23 store-management restructure did not publish a 7-to-5 layer count. Reads as a fabricated specific.' That verdict REQUIRES failing to find external evidence. No stage in this nine-stage design can issue a lookup. The largest failure class is allocated zero retrieval and the design calls it 'probabilistically caught'. The honest word is 'not caught'.

NO BRIEF OWNS DIAGRAMS, AND THE CENSUS CANNOT NOTICE. 81 diagrams across 43 sections carry 17 logged accuracy issues, 6 of them high. R1 owns spec/tariff, R2 quotes sentences (an SVG path is not a sentence, and quote-check.mjs byte-matching makes path findings awkward), R3 sees only student-visible items with prose withheld, R4 owns sequencing. Diagrams are an unowned class -- and S4 check (1) only compares reviewedItemCount to section-index counts 'for the classes it owns', so an unowned class passes the census by construction, silently. S7 cannot cover it either: two text scripts and a grader means drawn-diagram marks, a large share of WEC12/WEC13 analysis marks, are invisible. And the S3 canary recipe list contains no diagram mutation, so the scoreboard reads 100% per-brief recall on a section whose long-run perfect-competition diagram draws supernormal profit.

S4 CHECK (3) IS ARITHMETICALLY BROKEN AND WILL BE RELAXED WITHIN FIVE SECTIONS. Pass = R3's blind score 'within 10 points of chance (25%)', i.e. a 15-35% window. An Opus-class model answering IAL AS-level MCQs from stem and options alone scores 70-90% because it knows the economics. The condition conflates 'guessable from surface features' (a construction defect) with 'answerable from subject knowledge without the prose' (which every exam-valid item is). So a PERFECT section fails S4 forever. The predictable response at 11pm is to widen the threshold, and at that moment the answer-B detector -- the design's proudest number -- stops measuring anything. Worse, the thing it is supposed to catch (492 of 769 keys on index B; longest option correct in 15 of 25 in entrepreneurs-leaders) is a ten-line chi-square that belongs in S1 for free. An agent is being spent on the one check that did not need one, under a threshold that cannot pass.

THE PIPELINE IS CONTENT-INDEXED; 340 SPEC GAPS (29% of all 1,170 findings) ARE ABSENCE. Every stage starts from the section and walks outward. Nothing starts from the spec and walks in. R1's input is a 'spec extract' -- if that extract is retrieved by keyword from the section it is circular, and a bullet the section never mentions never enters the extract. Census arithmetic is definitionally inapplicable to items that do not exist: you cannot subtract your way to a missing subsection. price-determination: '1.3.4 3(b) The price mechanism in the context of different types of markets, including local, national and global markets - not taught anywhere (no subsection, no example, no recall, no MCQ).' The only cover offered is S1's 'spec-bullet keyword map', which is simultaneously the most gameable rule in the design -- the authoring agent satisfies it by sprinkling the words, which is exactly the meeting-customer-needs guidance-padding failure the design already cites against itself.

CROSS-ARTEFACT CONTRADICTION HAS NO OWNER, NO CENSUS AND NO CANARY. Every pass condition in S4 counts ITEMS; contradictions are PAIRS, and no brief's reviewedItemCount rises for checking block-0 prose against quiz item 13. national-income (critical): examMatters teaches transfer payments are G and an injection while 'quiz[13] in this very section says transfer payments are excluded from GDP... A student following the examMatters would lose the mark quiz[13] awards.' market-failure (critical): 'Q5 in the same bank explicitly keys the correct answer... Q18's own explanation contradicts its option text. A pre-test can draw Q5 and Q18 together and mark opposite things right.' aggregate-demand (critical): keyIdea says consumption is 'the largest and most volatile component of AD', contradicted by the next subsection's keyIdea and two block takeaways in the same file. R3 structurally cannot see any of these -- its brief withholds the teaching prose, which is half of every pair.

THE CENSUS MEASURES ENUMERATION, NOT REVIEW, AND ITS DENOMINATORS ARE CONSTANTS. Every one of the 43 sections has exactly 5 practice items (215/43) and quiz caps at 25 (median 24). So 'reviewedItemCount equals the artefact counts' reduces to 'the agent emitted 5 rows and 25 rows'. An agent producing 25 shallow rows passes identically to one producing 25 deep rows. March's failure was not skipping items; it was passing them shallowly behind a validator that counted things. This is the design's headline anti-rubber-stamp mechanism and it reproduces the exact epistemics of the string-length validator, one level up.

S3 IS LABELLED 'Objective, arithmetic, no judgement' AND IS NOT. Deciding that an injected mutation IS a defect, and that it sits at the difficulty of a real one, is judgement. The only calibration in the design is negative -- 'S1 must not see it'. Nothing establishes a canary is as hard as the Saudi Arabia supply inversion or the AC-curve geometry error. So S6 divides a caught-count by a denominator of unknown difficulty and the design markets the quotient as 'the gate's own error rate is a measured number rather than a hope'. It is a measured number of the wrong thing, and its most likely failure mode is reading high, which is the mode that authorises shipping.

FREE ARITHMETIC IS MISSING WHILE AGENTS ARE DEPLOYED. the-market quiz (critical): '500x$40 = $20,000; 400x$50 = $20,000' yet the key says 'demand is inelastic so revenue rises', and the shipped explanation contains a visible authoring note -- 'Revenue rises from $20,000 to $20,000... actually revenue = ... However...'. financial-planning quiz (critical): 'Options [0] and [2] are both £500... a student picking [2] is marked wrong for the right answer', and it is the inline MCQ every Learn Mode user hits. trade-global-economy (critical): the comparative-advantage panel goes 70 wheat + 30 cars to 40 wheat + 50 cars while checklist[2] demands 'total world output increases'. None of these needs an agent, a spec or a mark scheme. They are absent because S1's rule set was enumerated from March's already-found findings -- it is a snapshot of known defects, not a class of checks, which is precisely the property that let March's validator pass 43 sections.
wouldLetThrough: market-structures-contestability diagrams[1] (high): 'Perfect Competition -- Long-Run Equilibrium ... The AR = MR = P line at y=160 lies above AC everywhere (AR > AC), so the diagram depicts supernormal profit, not the tangent at minimum AC, normal profit only the checklist claims.' Unowned class, no static geometry rule, no canary recipe, invisible to a text-script ablation. Ships with a 100% scoreboard.

market-structures-contestability diagrams[2] (high): monopoly MR=MC intersection is at approximately (205,193) but 'the MR=MC dot is at (210,170) -- ~23px above the intersection'; the DWL apex is placed where AR is at y=177 and MC at y=88. Same hole.

causes-effects-globalisation diagrams[1] (high): 'the Reasons for FDI column occupies x=10-140, y=100-257, while the Positive (+) impact boxes occupy x=60-230, y=153-273. They overlap... four reason labels and four positive-impact labels render on top of each other and the diagram is unreadable.' S1 checks dangling refs, not whether the picture renders.

managing-people realExample (high): 'Marks & Spencer restructured its hierarchy in 2022, reducing management layers from seven to five -- could not be corroborated... Reads as a fabricated specific.' A plausible invented number with no contradicting text in any model's weights passes R2, R4, S5, S7 and S8 unchanged.

planning-raising-finance realExample (high): Tesla gigafactory 'funded with government loans and retained profits' -- 'Tesla's US DOE loan ($465m, 2010, repaid 2013) funded the Fremont plant, not the Gigafactory... Tesla had no retained profits (cumulative losses until 2020). The narrative is invented.' Requires a lookup. No stage has one.

assessing-competitiveness realExample (high): 'Tesla's ROCE went from negative figures in 2019 to over 25% by 2023' -- actually ~11-12% in FY2023. A date-shifted true fact is the single hardest shape for a weights-only checker and the easiest for a one-line retrieval.

resource-management realExample (high): the Toyota JIT inversion -- 'Toyota was widely reported as the carmaker LEAST affected by the chip shortage precisely because it broke from pure JIT for semiconductors.' The design names this as what S7 catches AND, in its own 'admits it misses' list, as the claim that 'passes every stage'. Both cannot be true. S7's grader check is the same weights that find the inverted story plausible, so the second statement is the correct one and S7's headline claim is false.

national-income (critical): examMatters teaches transfer payments are an injection while quiz[13] in the same section excludes them from GDP. Per-item census, no pair denominator, R3 blind to the prose half.

price-determination specGap: '1.3.4 3(b) The price mechanism in the context of different types of markets... not taught anywhere (no subsection, no example, no recall, no MCQ).' Nothing assesses it either, so no untaught-assessment rule fires. Pure absence in a content-indexed pipeline.

aggregate-supply realExample (high): 'UK manufacturers in early 2022 saw margins boosted and expanded production because wages lagged output prices... The example illustrates the opposite of what happened.' Plausible, internally coherent, contradicted only by external data.

the-market quiz (critical): the elasticity item whose own arithmetic refutes its key, shipping with the authoring note 'Revenue rises from $20,000 to $20,000... actually revenue = ... However...' still in the explanation string. No S1 rule, and R3 reports only a score, never a disagreement.

52 of 340 spec gaps are hedged by the September reviewer itself -- 'in the WEC13 spec I recall', 'my recollection is', 'Unsure -- flag for verification against the current spec PDF' -- written while bus_spec.txt (130KB) and econ_spec.txt (156KB) sat in the same directory unread. That is a measured 15% don't-actually-know rate on spec claims from the exact reviewer population this gate re-hires, and S5's 'verbatim evidence that re-finds in the file' validates quotes from the SECTION, so a hedged claim about the SPEC quotes nothing and cannot be falsified by re-finding.
critiques.costRealism:
"Tokens: honest. I measured it. Median section JSON is 93KB (mean 92KB, max 156KB), so ~25-30k tokens of section alone; 4 briefs x ~100k + 10-25 skeptics x 10k + 30k seeder + 60k ablation lands at 0.6-0.8M per section, inside the stated 0.4-1.0M, and 43 x ~0.7M is ~30M. The design is also right to flag this against PROTOCOL.md line 117 ('Anything expected to cost more than a few million subagent tokens is checked with the founder first') -- 30M is an order of magnitude over that rule and needs approval before section one, not discovery at section ten.

Founder minutes: NOT honest, in four separate ways.

(1) 12 minutes is per ATTEMPT, presented as per SECTION. 'Any no reopens the section' with no bound on reopens and no accounting for the second look. With ~10 accuracy issues per section in March and a 44% realExample defect rate, early reopen rates will be high and the real figure is 12 x (1 + expected reopens).

(2) Question (c) 'does that mark look right for that script?' is an examiner judgement, posed to the person the founder explicitly ruled out as unqualified. The design removes the examiner and then asks the non-examiner the examiner's question. Reading a 20-mark levels-marked IAL script (400-600 words) plus its question plus a level grid carefully is 5-8 minutes on its own for a non-examiner; the remaining three artefacts do not fit in the other 4-7.

(3) The sample is 4 artefacts against a median section of ~70 (median 8 subsections, 24 quiz, 5 practice, 2 diagrams, 18 flashcards, 5 notes, 4 chains, 3 eval) -- 5.7% of one section, ~6% of the corpus across 43. And the one random realExample is drawn from a class with a 44% logged defect rate (182 issues across 413 realExamples): he is shown a coin flip from the worst class, with no answer key and no lookup, and asked 'is this claim true'. He cannot know that M&S went from seven layers to five. Nobody can, without searching.

(4) Total honest cost: 43 x 12 + 5 x 33 extra = ~11.4 founder-hours steady state, before reopens. The ruled-out plan was 20-40 hours of paid examiner time. So this design does not eliminate the cost -- it moves 30-60% of it onto the scarcest, least qualified person in the loop, and does not say so. The design should state that number up front and defend it, because 11 hours of unqualified attention is a worse buy than 20 hours of qualified attention if the founder can find any way to pay for the latter."
changes: ADD A RETRIEVAL STAGE, OR BAN UNVERIFIABLE SPECIFICS. Cheapest first: change the realExample schema from {text, emoji} to {text, emoji, source: {url, publisher, retrieved, claim}} and make S1 BLOCK any realExample containing a named organisation AND a year AND a figure without a resolving source. That converts the single largest failure class (182/453) from an unsolved judgement problem into a static check at zero agent cost. Then add S4.5 CORROBORATOR: one agent with web access, whose only census is the extracted claim list (entity+date+figure triples, ~10 per section), and whose verdicts are 'fetched and confirmed' / 'fetched and contradicted' / 'could not corroborate'. 'Could not corroborate' must delete or genericise the claim, never retain it. Without this the gate does not touch 40% of the accuracy class and the founder's bar is unreachable.

GIVE DIAGRAMS AN OWNER AND A STATIC RULE SET. Add R5 DRAUGHTSMAN with the diagram census as its denominator (81 diagrams, section-index counts them already). Before that, add S1 rules that are pure arithmetic over the SVG: sample every path at N points and assert declared curvature (a PPF asserted concave must be concave; an AC curve must be U-shaped, not fall-rise-fall); assert every marked intersection dot lies within tolerance of the actual path intersection (this alone catches the 23px monopoly error, the 22px monopsony error and the PC tangency error); assert declared profit relations (AR vs AC at the marked equilibrium); assert no two labelled boxes overlap (catches the FDI diagram); assert axis-label agreement between SVG, checklist and body (Qe vs Qm, Yf vs Yfe, P*/Q* vs Pe/Qe); and require any numeric axis to carry a source. Add a diagram mutation to the canary bank. Until this exists the scoreboard is measuring recall on a corpus subset that excludes the class with the highest known defect rate.

REPLACE S4(3). Delete the absolute blind-score threshold -- it cannot pass. Replace with an invariance test: R3a answers the bank as authored; R3b answers the same bank with options shuffled and relabelled. Defect signal is the DELTA and the residual correlation between key position and correctness, not the score. Simultaneously move position skew and longest-option-correct into S1 as a chi-square over each 25-item bank (free, deterministic, already known to fire on 492/769 keys). And note that the answer-B exploit is partly a RENDERER defect -- entrepreneurs-leaders explicitly says 'Verify whether InlineQuiz/PreTest shuffle; if not, re-balance'. Fix the shuffle in InlineQuiz/PreTest as a one-line product change before spending 43 sections re-balancing keys; re-balancing keys is exactly the mechanical compliance the design predicts an authoring agent will produce.

ADD A SPEC-INDEXED STAGE THAT WALKS FORWARD. R1 must be given the FULL unit spec (econ_spec.txt is 156KB, ~40k tokens -- affordable, and it is sitting unread in audit/raw/), not a section-derived extract, and its census denominator must be SPEC BULLETS OWNED BY THIS SECTION, not section artefacts. For each bullet it emits taught / assessed-only / absent plus the quoted subsection that teaches it. This is the only way absence becomes countable, and it closes the 340-finding blind spot. Keyword maps do not substitute: they are the most gameable rule in the design.

SEED CANARIES FROM REAL MARCH DEFECTS, NOT FROM RECIPES. audit/raw/content-audits.json holds 453 accuracy, 398 quiz and 224 practice issues, already severity-graded and already written by an examiner-level reviewer. Build the canary bank by transplanting actual logged defects into new sections rather than inventing mutations. This gives canaries measured real-world difficulty, kills the 'same model family writes both the canary and the reviewer' objection on the seeder side, and makes the S6 quotient interpretable. Also delete the claim that S3 is 'objective, arithmetic, no judgement' -- it is not, and pretending otherwise is how a measured error rate becomes a hope again.

MAKE THE CENSUS MEASURE DEPTH. Every census row must carry a verbatim quote from the item and a typed verdict (ok / defect / uncertain-needs-lookup). Extend quote-check.mjs from cited findings to all census rows -- it already exists and already caught 2 of 88 mis-citations. Without this, 'reviewedItemCount equals 5 practice and 25 quiz' is satisfied by emitting rows, and since those denominators are literally constant across all 43 sections it is the weakest possible check.

ADD A CONTRADICTION PASS WITH A PAIR DENOMINATOR. Extract every assertive claim in the section (keyIdea, body, examMatters, takeaway, quiz key, quiz explanation, flashcard, misconception) into a typed claim list, then run one agent whose census is CLAIM PAIRS sharing an entity, not items. This is the only shape that catches national-income, aggregate-demand and market-failure Q5-vs-Q18, and it is the class where a model with no external knowledge is genuinely reliable, because both halves of the contradiction are in the file.

ADD THE FREE CHECKS S1 IS MISSING, AND WRITE THEM AS CLASSES NOT INSTANCES: duplicate or near-duplicate MCQ options (catches financial-planning's two '£500's); arithmetic consistency between any figures in a stem and the claim in the key or explanation (catches the-market's 500x$40 = 400x$50 revenue item, and the 70/30 to 40/50 comparative-advantage panel); authoring-residue lint ('actually', 'However...', trailing ellipses, unterminated sentences, TODO, placeholder currency) in any student-visible string; and currency/notation consistency per subject. Then require every future S1 rule to be added as a class with a stated denominator, so the rule set stops being a snapshot of March.

FIX S8. Drop question (c) entirely -- it asks a self-declared non-examiner to do examiner work on a sample of one, and the design's own evidence (6 of 10 mechanism claims false) argues he should not be the arbiter of a level judgement. Replace with a symptom question he is genuinely reliable on: 'would you put this in front of a paying student?' Raise the realExample sample from 1 to 5 and show them with their sources attached, so his check becomes 'does this source say this' rather than 'do you happen to know'. Re-budget honestly at 25 minutes per attempt, publish the ~11-hour total against the ruled-out 20-40 examiner hours, and let the founder decide with the real number in front of him.

STOP CALLING THE SCOREBOARD AN ERROR RATE UNTIL IT COVERS THE CORPUS. Per-brief recall against 6 canaries per section, on a corpus with a ~44% realExample defect rate and a ~21% diagram defect rate, will read high while both classes leak. Publish it with its denominator and its excluded classes printed alongside -- the same discipline S1 already applies when it prints 'the list of classes it did NOT check'. Apply that rule to S6 too, or the one artefact in this design that is supposed to prevent self-deception becomes its main vehicle.

SHIP THE TWO THINGS THAT ARE ALREADY RIGHT, IMMEDIATELY AND SEPARATELY. S1's write-path proxy in scripts/_db.mjs plus the provenance lint, and S2's anchor census against the 72 real mark schemes (the 'observed at least twice' rule that rejects 173 of 215 live items) are the strongest parts of this design and the only genuinely objective ones alongside S9. They do not depend on any of the above. And close the world-readable Supabase bucket serving 86 Pearson PDFs today, as the design says -- that is a legal exposure sitting outside this entire argument.

1. SPEND 20 FOUNDER MINUTES ON S0 BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE. Print 10 randomly-sampled Shape Bank rows with paper code, session and question number; the founder opens those PDFs and confirms command, tariff and band boundaries. Record per-row pass/fail in the committed artefact; any mismatch halts S0. This is the highest-leverage founder minute available and the design currently spends zero there, on the artefact all 43 sections inherit.

2. FIX audit/raw/section-index.json BEFORE S3 EVER RUNS. It reports mistakes: 0 for all 43 sections against 188 actual items. Regenerate it from the section files at build time and assert that every top-level array in a section file has an inventory key. Until then the census check arithmetically rewards a reviewer for skipping an entire artefact class.

3. REPLACE S2's CHI-SQUARE-AS-PASS WITH A HARD BOUND: no option index may hold more than 40% of keys, and refuse the test entirely for banks under 20 items (19 of 43 sections). A non-significance result is not evidence of balance.

4. DELETE 'MCQ score <= 35%' AS A PASS CONDITION and add a separate key-verification stage: an agent answers each MCQ from first principles with both the section AND the key hidden; every disagreement with the key is a finding, not a score. As written, wrong keys help you pass, and nothing else in the gate verifies a quiz key.

5. DELETE 'the agent's reported cue list is empty' as a pass condition. It is an agent self-report - the exact 'a reviewer says it is good' construction the founder banned. Keep it as a diagnostic only.

6. ADD S2b, CLOSED-WORLD CONSISTENCY: one agent, section JSON only, enumerating every pair of claims in the file that cannot both be true (keyIdea vs takeaway vs misconception vs common_mistakes vs quiz explanation vs body). 75 of March's findings are in this class; it needs no examiner, no spec and no PDF. Critically, this is the ONE class where canaries can be generated mechanically at arbitrary volume (flip a takeaway to contradict its keyIdea), which converts the design's admitted '18 canaries, cannot estimate recall' problem into a measured recall number. Run it on packet 14 and report that number - it is the only recall figure this design can actually produce.

7. RE-SCOPE S4. Its pass condition reads the exact lever the adversary is observed to pull. Require any critical/high downgrade to pass a second adversary that sees only the finding and the proposed severity; surface every downgrade as a line on the S6 founder page, not as a ledger row; cap DEBT per packet.

8. ADD A PLACEBO ARM TO S5 BEFORE TRUSTING IT: a third condition given only the section's headings and key terms, no prose. If placebo-minus-blind also clears +15pp, S5 measures keyword cueing of a model that already knows the syllabus, not teaching, and the invented +15pp threshold must be re-derived. 3 agents, once. Cheapest possible falsification of the design's central claim.

9. MAKE THE examMatters RULE A SUPPORT CHECK, NOT A PRESENCE CHECK. Either commit the mark-scheme indicative content needed to support content-level claims (and accept the copyright position that entails), or ban 'Examiners reward/penalise X' sentences outright and replace them with the facts you actually hold: command, tariff, AO split, whether a recommendation is required. Never let a facts-only citation launder a claim it cannot support.

10. SANDBOX THE REVIEWERS FROM THE REPO, EXPLICITLY. S3 says R2 gets 'the section JSON only', but agents here have filesystem access by default and audit/canary-log.json is committed. An unsandboxed reviewer can find the canaries, and canary recall then reads 100% while real recall stays unknown. Also state the reuse: 3 canaries x 43 sections from a bank of 18 means each canary is used ~7 times, so recall degrades into memorisation across packets.

11. ADD TO S1: duplicate-option detection (financial-planning Q3 has two '£500' options, only one keyed, and it is the inline MCQ every Learn Mode user in that block hits) and unanswerable-stem detection (external-influences Q15's '$1 = $1.30 to $1 = $1.40'). Make a missing `command` field a BLOCK, not a skip - 50 of 215 live practice items have no command, so the (subject, unit, command, marks) key is incomplete for 23% of them, and a validator that skips rows it cannot key IS the March validator.

12. CHANGE THE PILOT SECTION. Run packet 14 on introductory-concepts, not a mid-traffic one. It is the highest-traffic section (192 users vs 123 for meeting-customer-needs) AND it is in the 5-section zero-anchor set where the author admits the central bet is not being made. Prove the gate where it is weakest and matters most, or packet 14 teaches you nothing transferable.

13. SPEND AN HOUR ON INSTRUMENTATION BEFORE PACKET 14. user_quiz_attempts has 0 rows, user_content_progress has 0 rows, Learn Mode has 0 recorded completions. The author says the terminal question is undecidable because it 'needs a cohort and a term'; it is also undecidable because nothing is being recorded. Fix the recording now and every stage above becomes falsifiable later at zero extra cost. Leave it and this gate is permanently an opinion.

14. KEEP AND EXTEND THE TWO BEST IDEAS: the success report that never prints the word 'passed' and that lists what it did NOT check. Apply that to every stage, not just S1, and commit the author's honest status line verbatim per section.
critiques.costRealism: "Partly honest, wrong in both denominator and scope. DENOMINATOR: the design says the founder sees 'roughly four of about sixty items per section'. I counted the real inventory in audit/content-sections/ - median 244 independently falsifiable claims per section (413 at the top, economics__measures-economic-performance; 132 at the bottom, business__influences-business-decisions), counting each quiz option and each explanation as the separate claim it is. Even on the most conservative count (one claim per quiz item) it is ~128. So S6 samples ~1.6%, not the ~6.7% claimed - understated by 2-4x. The '1 in 10 defective means he sees one about a third of the time' arithmetic is correct (1-0.9^4 = 34%) but describes sampling, not recognition. SCOPE: 2 of the 5 prompts ask him to adjudicate external-world facts ('Warby Parker grew to a $3 billion valuation through direct distribution alone'). audit/raw/research-founder-report-factcheck.md says of his own report: 'Roughly a third of the report is grounded observation and two-thirds is speculation dressed as diagnosis... the things a user can see are directionally right; but nearly every mechanistic explanation attached to them is invented.' S6 declares 'symptoms only, never mechanism' and then breaks that rule on 40% of its own prompts - and the DELETE rule then fires on the unreliable signal, while a 'looks-right' on a fabrication ships it with founder approval attached. WORSE, THE SAMPLING CRITERION IS PUBLISHED: S6 samples realExamples 'flagged as named-entity-plus-year-plus-figure', so an authoring agent optimising against the gate writes examples without a year or a figure. The sample suppresses the flag, not the falsehood. OMISSIONS: zero founder minutes on S0, the artefact all 43 sections inherit; no defined founder branch for 3 of 5 prompts (DELETE is specified only for factual claims - what happens when the authored practice item 'looks-wrong' next to the real stem is undefined); no time budgeted for arbitrating BLOCK-vs-DEBT, which is precisely where March-by-downgrade lives; no re-entry cost when a deleted realExample forces re-authoring and re-gating. 12 x 43 = 8.6 hours is affordable. It is allocated to the wrong minutes. CONTEXT THE FIGURE IGNORES: audit/raw/engagement_aggregates.json shows 44 distinct practice users, 3 active in the last 7 days, 16 premium/active, 0 rows in user_quiz_attempts, 0 rows in user_content_progress, 0 Learn Mode completions - and funnel_aggregates shows 167 of 192 users on introductory-concepts never leave step 0. ~15 agents and 12 founder minutes per section is being spent on exam-alignment of content that 87% of arriving users never reach past the first screen."
fatalFlaws: S0'S SHAPE BANK IS AN UNVERIFIED ORACLE THAT ALL 43 SECTIONS INHERIT, AND THIS REPO SHIPPED EXACTLY THAT FAILURE FOUR DAYS AGO. audit/PROTOCOL.md: 'a wrong version of this table was propagated to 52 agents on 12 September.' The --verify assertions are all structural - >=2 sightings, 72/72 files yield, no shared 8-gram, coverage flags, regenerated command_words - and none of them check that a parsed row is CORRECT. A parser that reads a band boundary off the neighbouring grid, or associates a tariff with the wrong question, produces two cited sightings and passes all five assertions. Not one row is ever read by a human. The design spends 12 founder minutes per section on samples and zero on the single artefact every section is anchored to.

S3'S CENSUS INVENTORY IS WRONG TODAY, AND WRONG IN THE DIRECTION THAT REWARDS THE LAZY REVIEWER. audit/raw/section-index.json reports mistakes: 0 for all 43 of 43 sections; the section files contain 188 common_mistakes (3-6 each). Every other inventory key matches. So 'each reviewer's enumerated item count equals the inventory in section-index.json' FAILS the reviewer who enumerates common_mistakes and PASSES the one who skips all 188 of them. The design's single strongest anti-laziness mechanism currently enforces the laziness it was built to prevent, over an artefact class the March audit found defects in.

S2'S PASS CONDITIONS ARE ANTI-CORRELATED WITH QUIZ CORRECTNESS AND STATISTICALLY POWERLESS ON HALF THE CORPUS. (a) 'MCQ score <= 35%' is monotonically IMPROVED by wrong answer keys: a blind agent reasoning correctly on supply Q21 or market-failure Q18 is scored wrong and pushed toward the pass threshold. The one stage touching quiz integrity rewards bad keys. (b) 'chi-square p > 0.05' is a pass on FAILING TO REJECT, so it gets easier as banks shrink. I computed it: n=10 keyed [6,2,2,0] - 60% on one option - gives chi2=7.60, p=0.055, PASSES. n=25 keyed [12,5,4,4] - 48%, nearly double chance - gives p=0.067, PASSES. 19 of 43 sections have 9-12 quiz items. The live corpus sits at 64% and the audit called that critical; this test would wave through 60%. (c) 'the agent's reported cue list is empty' is an agent self-report - literally 'a reviewer says it is good'.

S4 IS A SEVERITY-LAUNDERING STAGE AND THE DESIGN PUBLISHES THE PROOF. Pass = 'zero findings left open at corrected severity critical or high'. Observed adversary behaviour, stated by the author: 'on the 88 code verdicts it refuted 6, all of them severity overturns, and killed 0 findings on fact.' The adversary's only demonstrated capability is severity adjustment, and severity is the exact quantity the gate reads. March did not happen because someone bypassed a check; the next March happens with a green gate and a ledger full of DEBT that used to be critical.

NOTHING IN THE GATE CHECKS THE SECTION AGAINST ITSELF. 75 of the 453+398+224 March findings are internal contradictions: retained profit has 'no cost' in the body while the misconception in the same subsection says calling it free is wrong; JIT 'eliminates stock-holding costs' in the takeaway while its own misconception says JIT firms hold a buffer; aggregate-demand's keyIdea says consumption 'is the largest and most volatile component of AD' while the next subsection's keyIdea, the block takeaway and block 5's takeaway all say investment is; aggregate-demand's body defines MPC one way and quiz Q21 marks the resulting formula WRONG. This class needs no examiner, no spec, no PDF and no external truth - and there is no stage for it. It is the cheapest high-yield check available and it is absent.

THE examMatters CITATION RULE CANNOT WORK, BECAUSE S0 DESTROYS THE ONLY EVIDENCE THAT COULD SUPPORT IT. The Shape Bank is facts-only - command, tariff, AO split, band boundaries, ceilings, QS codes - and 'stem text is read to derive topic tags and then discarded'. Mark-scheme indicative content is never committed. So 'Examiners penalise students who draw MSC above MPC for a consumption externality' (market-failure, graded high, and false) can carry a Shape Bank citation that is structurally valid and semantically empty. The rule upgrades an unsourced claim into a falsely-sourced one, which is worse: the 244 uncited 'Examiners reward' sentences are at least visibly uncited.

UNRESOLVED CONTRADICTION IN THE COPYRIGHT STORY. S1 validates 'the payload being written, plus... the n-gram index of the 86 texts', but extraction happens in a gitignored workspace and the claim is that 'the repo never carries the protected material'. Either the 8-gram index IS committed - and an 8-gram index of full text is substantially a reconstructable representation of that text, i.e. the exposure you claimed to eliminate - or it is not, in which case S1 cannot run in CI or on any other machine and 'validator-sweep green on all 43 sections' is not a reproducible gate condition. As written the design cannot be both things it claims.
critiques.verdict: "adopt with changes - but do not run packet 14 as written"
wouldLetThrough: global-marketing, flashcards[11] and common_mistakes[4] (Chevrolet Nova): the 'no va' story is 'a well-documented myth: the car sold adequately in Venezuela and Mexico', and 'common_mistakes[4] even builds a recommendation on it'. Sits in the census blind spot (mistakes: 0 in section-index.json) AND in the admitted fact-check gap. Two independent failures of the gate on one item.

economics national-income, CRITICAL: teaches that transfer payments are government spending (G) and an injection - 'these are government spending (injection) even though they are not payment for output'. Conceptual, not shape. The term is taught so term-presence passes; it is on-spec so the keyword map passes; it is not one of the five denylist terms; a mark scheme rewards answers, it does not teach, so the anchor gives no oracle. The author admits this class; this is the worst instance of it.

economics aggregate-demand, CRITICAL: keyIdea states consumption 'is the largest and most volatile component of AD' while the very next subsection's keyIdea, the block takeaway and block 5's takeaway all say investment is the most volatile. Pure within-file contradiction. No stage owns it.

business the-market, CRITICAL: the UK strawberry realExample is 'backwards and teaches the wrong concept' - presents a seasonal supply SHIFT as 'the law of supply in action' (movement along the curve), 'a textbook example of the opposite'. Correct tariff, on-spec topic, taught terms, no denylist hit. Only R2 and a 2-in-9.6 founder sample stand between this and a student.

economics supply Q21: keyed answer 'market price exceeds its average total costs' is wrong or at best contestable (the shut-down rule is AVC; the supply condition is P = MC). economics market-failure Q18: the keyed answer for deadweight loss is 'WRONG: that area (MSC-MPC from 0 to Qm) is the total external cost' and directly contradicts Q5 in the SAME bank and Q18's own explanation. Nothing in the gate verifies a quiz key, and both of these would LOWER a blind agent's score, making S2 easier to pass.

business financial-planning Q3: options [0] and [2] are both '£500', only [0] keyed - 'a student picking [2] is marked wrong for the right answer', and it is 'the inline MCQ for the Cash-Flow block (quizIndices [3]), so every Learn Mode user hits it'. I confirmed this is the only duplicate-option item in the live corpus. It is one line of static code and the design's static list does not include it.

business external-influences Q15: 'Currency typo: should read £1 = $1.30 to £1 = $1.40. As written the stem is nonsensical and a student cannot tell which currency strengthened.' No stage in the design asks whether a stem is answerable at all.

Off-spec frameworks NOT on the five-term denylist, each asserted as examiner-rewarded: VRIO ('Examiners reward structured VRIO analysis' - assessing-competitiveness), Bartlett & Ghoshal (global-markets-expansion, 'AQA A-level 3.7.7 content'), Mendelow (influences-business-decisions, 'not named in the Edexcel IAL spec'), Porter's Five Forces (external-influences, 'the claim that examiners frequently use it is false'). The denylist is back-fitted to March's five known terms. It cannot catch the sixth, and the authoring agent is the same model class that imported these five.

business-objectives-strategy: 'Porter's Generic Strategies' with 'three strategies' where IAL uses 'Porter's Strategic Matrix', a 2x2. Right concept, wrong exam vocabulary, so students 'may not recognise the exam wording'. Not a denylist hit, not a spec-keyword gap (Porter IS in the bullet), not a shape defect. Invisible to every mechanical rule in S1.

assessing-competitiveness flashcards[1]: 'Net profit margin = (Operating profit ÷ Revenue) × 100% is wrong.' A false formula, in the artefact class the author himself notes drew only 7 findings across 844 flashcards - i.e. the class where the golden set is silent and no baseline exists.

132 of 272 audited recall widgets are rated trivial (66), weak-or-arbitrary-sequence (48) or not-orderable (18) - structurally valid, pedagogically worthless. S1's hint-prefix rule and S2's 'zero fill-ins from the hint alone' cover only the 51 hint-leaks-answer cases. No brief in S3 owns pedagogy (R1 examiner, R2 fact-checker, R3 spec-mapper), and S5 sits real past papers rather than our own widgets. Nearly half the recall corpus falls in a hole with no owner.

business managing-people: 'Paternalistic leadership is a named style in IAL 1.4.5 but is absent from the body, keyIdea, flow and recall - yet quiz Q5 (the block's inline quiz) asks for it.' The design's term-presence check is described as catching untaught assessment, and it would catch this one - but its mirror image, where the term IS present and the section teaches the opposite of what it tests (aggregate-demand MPC vs Q21), passes term-presence cleanly.
